title: Senator Probes Tether’s Reported $6M Deal With Firm Tied to Ex-Trump Crypto Advisor
summary: Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) has launched an investigation into Tether’s reported multimillion-dollar payments to a consulting firm co-owned by former White House cryptocurrency adviser Bo Hines, raising concerns about potential conflicts of interest and violations of federal ethics and lobbyin...
content:
Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) has launched an investigation into Tether’s reported multimillion-dollar payments to a consulting firm co-owned by former White House cryptocurrency adviser Bo Hines, raising concerns about potential conflicts of interest and violations of federal ethics and lobbying laws.

Key Takeaways

  • Sen. Richard Blumenthal is probing Tether’s reported $6.3 million payments to a consulting firm co-owned by former White House crypto adviser Bo Hines.
  • Blumenthal raised concerns that Hines may have influenced stablecoin legislation benefiting Tether while retaining an ownership stake in the firm.
  • Blumenthal requested contracts, payment records, and communications from Tether and the consulting firm by Nov. 6, citing potential ethics and lobbying violations.

Senator Blumenthal Seeks Answers From Tether

In an Oct. 22 letter to Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino, Blumenthal demanded records detailing the stablecoin issuer’s relationship with Nxum, a consulting firm co-founded by Hines, following a Wall Street Journal investigation that revealed the company allegedly received approximately $6.3 million from Tether while Hines helped shape crypto policy for President Donald Trump.

According to the Journal, Tether agreed in May 2025 to pay Nxum $415,000 monthly for strategic communications, lobbying, and public relations services. Hines retained a one-third ownership stake in the firm while serving as executive director of the White House Council of Advisers for Digital Assets.

Blumenthal alleged that Hines coordinated with Nxum through encrypted messaging applications while advocating for provisions in the GENIUS Act, the landmark stablecoin legislation signed into law in July 2025.

Those provisions reportedly included extending compliance deadlines and allowing foreign stablecoin issuers such as Tether greater flexibility to continue serving American customers.

The senator also questioned Tether’s unusual payment arrangements. Rather than contracting directly with Nxum, Tether allegedly routed cryptocurrency payments through another marketing firm, Notorious, before the funds were distributed to Nxum’s owners.

After Hines departed the White House in August 2025, Tether began contracting directly with Nxum and subsequently hired Hines to lead its newly established U.S. operations.

“The highly unusual terms and nature of Tether’s business relationship with both Nxum and Bo Hines raise alarming ethical and legal concerns,” Blumenthal wrote.

The Journal reported that Hines’ representatives denied he knew about or participated in the Tether deal while serving in government. Blumenthal also cited reports that Nxum has solicited additional investment by claiming Tether intends to purchase a 25% ownership stake in the firm for $56 million.

The senator requested contracts, cryptocurrency payment records, wallet addresses, and communications involving Tether, Nxum, Notorious and Hines. He sent a separate letter to Nxum CEO Todd Hines, Bo Hines’ father, seeking similar information.

Both companies have until Nov. 6 to respond.

The investigation adds to Blumenthal’s growing scrutiny of Tether and its political connections. Earlier this month, the senator demanded information from Cantor Fitzgerald about its financial relationship with Tether, following a congressional report alleging that the company’s USDT stablecoin facilitates transactions within Iran’s shadow banking network.

Cantor Fitzgerald, previously led by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and now controlled by his sons, owns a minority stake in Tether and manages substantial assets backing USDT.

Blumenthal’s latest inquiry focuses on whether Tether’s financial relationships with politically connected individuals improperly influenced federal cryptocurrency legislation. The allegations have not resulted in established findings of wrongdoing. Tether has yet to comment publicly on the investigation.

title: ‘CLARITY Is About as Good as You Can Get’—Byron Donalds Talks Bitcoin, Prediction Markets and Florida
summary: Byron Donalds wants governments to hold bitcoin, opposes a Federal Reserve-issued digital currency, and doubts federal agencies can keep pace with the markets they oversee. In an Oct. 17, 2026, interview with Bitcoin.com News, the Florida congressman and gubernatorial candidate discussed strategic r...
content:
Byron Donalds wants governments to hold bitcoin, opposes a Federal Reserve-issued digital currency, and doubts federal agencies can keep pace with the markets they oversee. In an Oct. 17, 2026, interview with Bitcoin.com News, the Florida congressman and gubernatorial candidate discussed strategic reserves, his race against former rep. David Jolly, and prediction markets that put his election chances close to 80%. His central warning was that Washington risks sending financial innovation and its economic rewards overseas.

Key Takeaways

  • Donalds outlined a Florida bitcoin reserve in his Oct. 17 interview, alongside fractional asset ownership.
  • At odds near 80%, Donalds said Polymarket offers daily trends, while ballots ultimately decide elections.
  • Looking 10 years ahead, Donalds warned that weak crypto rules would push investment and growth overseas.

Florida congressman and gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds wants Florida to build a bitcoin reserve, but the people writing the rules for digital assets don’t inspire much confidence in him. In a wide-ranging Oct. 17 interview with Bitcoin.com News, Donalds argued that governments should consider holding bitcoin while questioning whether lawmakers and regulators understand the financial machinery taking shape around them.

The conversation traveled from clients asking about a spare $1,000 to a proposed state reserve, hurricane insurance, and election contracts putting his chances around 80%. Throughout, Donalds returned to a question with consequences well beyond cryptocurrency: Who actually knows enough to call the shots?

From a Spare $1,000 to a Government Reserve

Before politics, Donalds worked in banking, finance, and insurance. His early encounters with bitcoin came through clients who wanted advice on something their financial adviser was still trying to size up himself.

“Most people hadn’t really researched it fully, and even clients would ask me, ‘Hey, what should I do with this stuff? Should I get into it?’” he recalled. “And I would say: If you have a spare thousand dollars and you want to buy a coin, go ahead.” Asked about its future, his answer then was straightforward: “Honestly, I didn’t really know.”

Today, he sees a different proposition. “I think bitcoin probably has more of a commodity feel now, but that being said, it’s obviously been proven to increase substantially in value,” Donalds said. “For the people who got in back in 2014, 2015, it worked out for them in a major way.”

Asked about legislation he introduced to put a strategic bitcoin reserve into federal law, he described bitcoin principally as a hedge. Everyday payments remain part of the picture, but he sees protection against monetary policy as its stronger selling point.

“But I definitely think it has a commodity play, and a hedge against central banking and monetary policy is probably its highest use, which gives it properties similar to gold,” he remarked. The congressman added:

“So in some respects it’s kind of like digital gold.”

Bitcoin.com News asked whether he supported budget-neutral acquisitions beyond bitcoin obtained through seizures. Donalds distinguished law enforcement seizures from deliberately assembling reserves, without laying out a purchase mechanism.

“But I do think trying to find ways for not just the federal government, but state governments, to begin to assemble a strategic reserve is important,” he said. “Governments going forward have to find ways to hedge against interest rate risk and other concerns, and I think this is a way to do that.”

He was less categorical about whether previous federal bitcoin sales were mistakes. He told Bitcoin.com News:

“It’s probably too early to say … You could say now it was a mistake, depending on the valuation they sold it at, but I think it was more about what the decision-making process was at that time.”

Congress Still Has Passbooks on Its Mind

Asked about the stablecoin-focused GENIUS Act and the CLARITY Act crypto market structure bill, Donalds singled out the Senate as the chief obstacle to a workable framework. His diagnosis was blunt, and it extended beyond the lawmakers themselves.

“The issue is that you have a bunch of senators who have no idea what this stuff really is, and their staff don’t know either,” he said. “So there’s a lot of misinformation and a lot of different viewpoints going around Capitol Hill, especially in the United States Senate.”

His remarks came on the heels of last month’s unsuccessful cloture vote, which brought the CLARITY Act’s legislative progress to a standstill. Donalds predicted the House would pass the same legislative package in the next Congress. He argued that some members of both chambers still approach finance through an outdated lens.

“But what we’re starting to see is a handful of members in the Senate, and also in the House, who, for the life of me, still think in terms of passbook savings accounts and balancing their savings ledger, as opposed to what the future of assets looks like,” he said.

He also questioned older lawmakers’ familiarity with cryptocurrency and decentralized finance (DeFi). His verdict on the legislation was measured against that limitation:

“CLARITY is about as good as you can get with the current iteration of Congress. I think you’re probably going to need new leaders who can actually get us there.”

A Florida Reserve, but No Central Bank Digital Currency

Government ownership of bitcoin gets his support. A central bank digital currency (CBDC) gets the opposite answer, driven by his concern about financial surveillance.

“I would never want the government to issue a digital currency where we’re supposed to trust that the government would never peer behind the curtain at the financial transactions of Americans,” Donalds said. “I would never support a central bank digital currency, and I never will.”

He said he would retain Florida’s CBDC prohibition enacted by Ron DeSantis. Donalds also accused opponents of CLARITY of supporting a CBDC. For Florida’s crypto industry, he identified two priorities.

“First of all, we actually have proposals to create a strategic reserve in Florida,” Donalds said. “I also think things around fractional exchanges, being able to have fractional ownership in real-world assets, are something Florida can definitely take a lead on.”

The latter means owning a portion of an asset rather than the whole thing. Donalds said Florida could promote digital assets used for investment and as derivatives tied to real-world property, though he did not outline specific rules or a timetable in the interview.

The Insurance Fight Comes Down to Who Pays

The conversation turned from digital assets to the bills Floridians face at home. In Florida’s gubernatorial contest, Donalds is squaring off against Democrat David Jolly, a former U.S. representative from the Sunshine State.

Asked about Jolly’s emphasis on affordability, property insurance, education, and health care, Donalds concentrated his criticism on insurance. The Jolly campaign features a property insurance proposal that seeks to remove hurricane and wind-related risks from the private insurance market altogether, consolidating that exposure within a single, state-backed catastrophic insurance fund.

Donalds weighed in on the proposal, offering his perspective:

“His insurance plan is a government takeover of wind insurance in Florida, and there are multiple problems with his proposal. The first is he doesn’t have the money to fund it.”

Donalds challenged the proposed funding sources, arguing that taxing insurers’ profits would become problematic if their business shifted to government. He also said tourist development taxes were local revenues totaling about $2 billion, and argued that redirecting them would require a state constitutional amendment.

His larger objection concerned the next hurricane. Donalds argued that removing policyholder assessments would leave the state borrowing heavily to pay claims, with residents eventually picking up the tab through taxes.

“If you’re not going to have the ability to assess policyholders, then the state of Florida will have to go borrow $30 billion in the bond market,” he said. “Think how much that would cost.” He warned that repeated storms would require repeated borrowing and called Jolly’s affordability approach “economic stupidity, not based in reality.”

Donalds offered his own target of reducing insurance bills by 20%. “We keep the tort reform supported by Governor DeSantis. We also make some structural reforms to our insurance market,” he said. “We make permitting automatic after storms, so when the storm leaves, people get an automatic permit to rebuild or rehabilitate their property.”

He disputed the idea that moving wind coverage into government hands would deliver savings of 60% to 70%, arguing that premiums or public borrowing would still finance the risk. He said:

“You end up taxing everybody anyway, and I don’t think that’s smart.”

Donalds Sees More Than an Election Bet

The interview then turned to markets trading on Donalds himself. Bitcoin.com News cited approximately 79% odds on Polymarket and 76% on Kalshi at the time of the conversation. The odds have since increased to 82% as of Oct. 23, 2026.

“I think they give you a better window into daily tracking. Polling just gives you a snapshot in time,” Donalds explained. “What you really want to look at is trend lines, and that’s what prediction markets give you.”

Still, he said ballots mattered more than favorable prices: “But at the end of it all, it’s always going to be about what people are doing. How are they going to show up and vote?” He attributed the market readings partly to what he described as the absence of a major Democratic ballot-return initiative in Florida.

Asked whether these markets were useful or essentially gambling, Donalds drew a distinction between a venue acting as the house and a marketplace matching opposing positions.

“But if you just have a marketplace where people take two sides of an issue, that’s a derivative contract, just like oil futures or orange juice futures or anything else,” he detailed.

He expected the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to prevail in jurisdictional disputes with states. “I largely think the CFTC is probably going to win out, but I could see some state regulatory guidance, probably much more around consumer protection,” Donalds explained.

A 10-Year Warning and a $4 Billion Résumé

Looking a decade ahead, Donalds defined policy failure as development and investment leaving the country because officials couldn’t establish workable rules. He paired his preference for industry growth with a call for basic consumer safeguards.

“I think failure is that a lot of the development in bitcoin, crypto markets, and prediction markets goes offshore, because Congress or the states can’t figure out regulatory systems that allow these industries to grow while making sure the average consumer has baseline protections that are just common sense,” he stressed.

Even a federal framework would leave another question, Donalds said: “Does the CFTC have the manpower and the intellectual capacity to truly regulate these marketplaces? Or do we just have regulations for regulation’s sake with no real ability to enforce them?”

Donalds said he had advocated industry self-regulation, including among Republican colleagues. “Let the industry create a regulatory framework, because whether it’s bitcoin, crypto, prediction markets, or tech overall, it’s moving so fast,” he emphasized. Asked whether he believes government capacity would improve, he answered, “No. Unfortunately, I don’t.”

He argued that the government responds too slowly to supervise these markets in real time. In closing, in terms of leading the state of Florida, Donalds described his campaign as super focused on housing, education, affordability, and government accountability. He pointed to his financial services career as the practical grounding for those ambitions.

“I was licensed. I managed a universal life insurance policy portfolio of about $4 billion,” he said. “At the start of my career, I was a credit analyst at a community bank, underwriting everything from housing starts to planned unit developments to commercial centers.”

He finished with the distinction he wants voters to remember, stating:

“Guiding Florida into the future is going to require a governor who knows economic policy, not just from a legal side, but from a real-world application side.”

title: Ethereum Delays Glamsterdam Testing After 13 Contracts Trigger Concerns
summary: Ethereum developers have postponed the Glamsterdam upgrade on the Hoodi testnet after security researchers discovered a flaw that could turn temporary smart contract failures into permanent losses of functionality. Chainsecurity identified 13 deployed contracts with potentially vulnerable behavior. ...
content:
Ethereum developers have postponed the Glamsterdam upgrade on the Hoodi testnet after security researchers discovered a flaw that could turn temporary smart contract failures into permanent losses of functionality. Chainsecurity identified 13 deployed contracts with potentially vulnerable behavior. The Oct. 26 activation has been canceled, putting Ethereum’s tentative December mainnet upgrade window in doubt while developers investigate.

Key Takeaways

  • Ethereum developers canceled Glamsterdam’s Oct. 26 Hoodi activation following security concerns.
  • Swiss blockchain cybersecurity and smart contract auditing firm Chainsecurity identified 13 deployed contracts vulnerable to potentially permanent failure states.
  • Ethereum’s tentative December launch faces uncertainty, but mainnet users need take no action.

Ethereum Delays Glamsterdam Testing After Security Flaws Threaten Contracts

Ethereum’s next major upgrade has hit an unexpected obstacle. Security researchers discovered that proposed changes to how the blockchain charges transaction fees can cause certain smart contracts to permanently record failures that previously would have been reversible.

Chainsecurity identified 13 deployed contracts exhibiting potentially dangerous behavior, prompting developers to cancel Glamsterdam’s Oct. 26 activation on the Hoodi test network. The discovery threatens an ambitious upgrade intended to make Ethereum faster and more efficient, with its tentative December launch now facing uncertainty.

A Security Discovery Forces Ethereum to Change Plans

During the Oct. 22 All Core Developers Execution meeting, developers agreed to postpone testing after reviewing findings involving two proposals, EIP-8037 and EIP-8038. The changes modify how the Ethereum protocol calculates gas, the fee mechanism that determines how much computing work a transaction can perform.

Chainsecurity found that certain operations might unexpectedly return previously consumed gas to a transaction. That seemingly helpful behavior creates a serious problem for smart contracts designed around existing spending limits.

When a Failed Transaction Becomes Permanent

Some smart contracts deliberately stop an operation when insufficient gas remains, allowing users to try again later. Under the proposed rules, however, a failed operation might leave enough gas for the surrounding contract to finish recording the failure. That can permanently disable a retry option or erase a user’s ability to claim funds.

The contract’s code wouldn’t necessarily need to change for the problem to appear. Researchers haven’t publicly identified the 13 affected contracts while responsible disclosure continues.

December Upgrade Window Faces Uncertainty

Glamsterdam combines improvements intended to increase Ethereum’s processing capacity and make block validation more efficient. Earlier testing on Sepolia succeeded on Oct. 6, with blocks operating near a 200 million gas limit, more than three times Ethereum mainnet’s roughly 60 million.

Hoodi operators must now install updated execution and consensus software before the canceled activation. Regular Ethereum users need take no action. The Ethereum Foundation hasn’t announced a replacement testing date or confirmed a mainnet launch. Developers must now determine whether changes intended to improve network performance can safely coexist with contracts already operating under older rules.

title: Argentine Court Clears President Milei of All Charges in Libra Crypto Case
summary: In a ruling issued Friday afternoon, charges against President Javier Milei, his sister Karina, and other defendants were dismissed after a court found that the losses associated with the launch of the Libra meme coin were not sufficient to constitute a scam. President Javier Milei and Others Acquit...
content:
In a ruling issued Friday afternoon, charges against President Javier Milei, his sister Karina, and other defendants were dismissed after a court found that the losses associated with the launch of the Libra meme coin were not sufficient to constitute a scam.

Key Takeaways

  • A court acquitted Argentine President Javier Milei of all fraud charges over the Libra meme coin collapse.
  • Judges found no proof of a scam, ruling Milei’s token promotion was personal and not an abuse of state power.
  • While 40,000 investors lost $110M, a separate trust plans to distribute the token’s proceeds as business grants.

President Javier Milei and Others Acquitted in Libra Meme Coin Case

President Javier Milei, his sister, and other defendants were acquitted of all charges regarding their involvement in the launch of Viva La Libertad Project (Libra), a meme coin focused on supporting small Argentine entrepreneurs launched back in February 2025.

The ruling, issued by the Buenos Aires National Criminal and Correctional Federal Court No. 8 on Friday afternoon and published by Argentine press, followed a petition from public prosecutor Eduardo Taiano, after determining that there was no conclusive evidence linking Milei or any defendants to the crimes alleged by the complainants.

Federal Judge Marcelo Martinez de Giorgi ruled that there was no evidence of a scam being carried out, as the Libra token was launched and blockchain data showed that it operated. Furthermore, there were no promises of future profitability, and the court specified that loss of funds on the volatile meme coin market was insufficient to prove a fraud actually happened.

Milei was linked to the Libra probe due to his promotion of the token on social media soon after its launch. Within hours, the token price plummeted, leaving over 40,000 investors affected and nearly $110 million in losses.

Regarding this promotion, the court found Milei did not commit abuse of authority crimes, as he shared the token information on a personal basis without resorting to institutional or administrative acts.

Finally, the court also dismissed charges of incompatible negotiations and influence peddling. In the ruling, the court stressed that it did not find evidence against Karina Milei, the president’s sister and General Secretary of the Presidency of the Argentine Nation, who was accused of receiving money to secure access and arrange meetings with President Milei.

The acquittal follows a similar ruling in New York, where a class action lawsuit involving RICO and other related charges against Kelsier Ventures and other defendants was dismissed earlier this month.

With these decisions, the Libra matter appears settled both in Argentina and the U.S., leaving no one responsible for the losses associated with the token dump. Nonetheless, an independent trust was launched in May to distribute over $110 million from Libra token sales to Argentine entrepreneurs before November, using a grants system. No further information has been provided about the distribution of these funds.

title: JPMorgan Expands Tokenized Money Market Funds To Solana
summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management says qualified U.S. investors can now access MONY and JLTXX tokenized money market funds on Solana through its Morgan Money platform.
content:
TL;DR: J.P. Morgan Asset Management says qualified U.S. investors can now access MONY and JLTXX tokenized money market funds on Solana through its Morgan Money platform.

J.P. Morgan Asset Management is bringing two of its tokenized money market funds to Solana, extending a traditional cash-management business across another public blockchain.

In an announcement Thursday, the investment manager said qualified U.S. investors can now access My OnChain Net Yield Fund, known as MONY, and the JPMorgan OnChain Liquidity–Token Money Market Fund, JLTXX, on Solana through its Morgan Money platform. Investors can subscribe and redeem through that institutional interface and receive balances represented at blockchain addresses.

Different funds, different investor rules

The two products are not identical forms of digital cash. MONY is a private placement offered under Rule 506(c), with eligibility restrictions for qualifying investors. JLTXX is a U.S.-registered government money market fund structured to serve cash management needs, including those of stablecoin issuers.

Both represent fund interests rather than ordinary deposit balances. J.P. Morgan's disclosures make clear that the funds are not bank accounts or FDIC-insured deposits, and that even products seeking a stable $1 share value can lose money.

That difference is easy to overlook when a token moves through a wallet interface. The blockchain record can make ownership and transfers more programmable; it does not change the underlying fund's investment objectives, regulatory status or redemption restrictions.

Why Solana now?

Institutions experimenting with tokenized assets increasingly operate across more than one chain. A fund that can be subscribed into on multiple networks may be more useful as a liquidity-management instrument, particularly when portfolio and treasury teams hold digital balances in different environments.

J.P. Morgan says adding Solana is intended to let clients access the same fund strategies across the networks where they operate. It is a distribution and settlement expansion, not the creation of two wholly new investment strategies.

The bank's Morgan Money platform remains central to the customer experience. That is significant because professional investors need controls that go beyond seeing a token balance, including eligibility screening, reporting, fund documents and predictable subscriptions and redemptions.

The company published Solana token addresses for both products, but copying a token identifier from social media is not a substitute for using the manager's verified onboarding channel. Token impersonation and lookalike assets remain a risk in on-chain markets.

For Solana, the listing adds another institutional financial product beyond speculative trading. For J.P. Morgan, it tests whether a familiar regulated fund structure can retain its governance while using a wider set of blockchain rails. Actual institutional adoption and transaction volumes, not the announcement alone, will show the importance of that change.

Source: www.prnewswire.com original announcement or data.

Related Reading: tokenized assets; crypto custody; stablecoins.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Wells Fargo and five others object to OKX-ICE tokenized stock listings: Report
summary: As of Friday, 22 companies had filed objections as part of the joint venture’s proposed tokenized stock platform under the SEC’s innovation exemption.
content:
Six more companies have reportedly filed objections to having their stocks listed in tokenized form on the proposed platform as part of a joint venture between cryptocurrency exchange OKX and the New York Stock Exchange’s parent company, the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE).

According to a Friday Reuters report, the proposed stock platform, called OKXICE, had 22 companies total objecting to having their US stock listings tokenized. Among the most recent objections reportedly included Wells Fargo, Arm Holdings and Intuit, adding their names to Microsoft and Google’s parent company Alphabet in the last week.

Notably, 16 of the companies were listed on Nasdaq, while only six of the stocks were available on the NYSE. Nasdaq released guidance for companies considering the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) innovation exemption for trading tokenized stocks in September, noting issuers “must be cautious about their participation,” saying “consequences for liquidity, price discovery, and long-term shareholder value may not become apparent until well after the experiment is underway.”

Speaking to Cointelegraph on Tuesday, OKXICE co-chair and former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo said that company expected there to be more objections in an effort to avoid being the first ones testing the stock model. The venture proposed 62 companies listing tokenized stocks when it filed with the SEC earlier this month.

Cointelegraph reached out to Intuit for comment on the company’s decision to opt-out of the initiative, but did not receive an immediate response. Spokespeople for Wells Fargo and Arm Holdings declined to comment.

Related: JPMorgan projects Bitcoin to outperform US stocks and gold over next decade

title: NY Seeks $1.37 Billion Judgment Against Operators of NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Scheme
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

NY Seeks $1.37 Billion Judgment Against Operators of NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Scheme
Two successive crypto frauds took investors for more than $1.1 billion. Now New York's attorney general is asking a court to make the operators pay it back—with interest.
This post NY Seeks $1.37 Bill...
content:
New York Attorney General Letitia James is trying to secure a $1.37 billion judgment against the operators of NovaTech and its predecessor AWS Mining, two successive cryptocurrency investment schemes that allegedly defrauded hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide out of more than $1 billion.

Alleged founders Cynthia and Eddy Petion never appeared in court and, according to the AG’s office, fled the country.

“NovaTech and AWS Mining scammed thousands of vulnerable New Yorkers by telling them they were making a safe investment when in reality, they were victims of a pyramid scheme,” James said in a statement. “These scammers targeted immigrant and religious communities with the promise of a better life but instead robbed them of their life savings.”

The schemes, AWS Mining and later NovaTech, relied on promoters who recruited heavily in Haitian and other immigrant communities — through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats, and ads in Haitian Creole.

AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts promising 15 to 20 percent monthly returns and 200 percent within 15 months. It collapsed in 2019. The Petions then launched NovaTech, marketed as a registered hedge fund broker, promising weekly trading returns of two to four percent — more than 140 percent a year.

Those returns were fabricated, according to prosecutors. Records from B2Broker, which supplied NovaTech’s white-label trading platform, show that of the more than $1 billion investors deposited between 2019 and 2023, only about $26 million was ever actually traded — and NovaTech’s traders lost $18.2 million of that. Returns to earlier investors came from newer deposits, not trading. When NovaTech collapsed in mid-2023, tens of thousands of investors could not withdraw their funds.

The AG is also seeking $134.5 million the Petions allegedly withdrew to their own wallets from the investor account Cynthia Petion solely controlled, plus $4.7 million tied to the earlier AWS Mining scheme. A default judgment entered in August 2025 already bars the couple and their companies from the securities, commodities, and cryptocurrency industries.

Separately, four of the scheme’s top promoters have agreed to pay nearly $6 million in disgorgement to victims and accepted the same industry bans.

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Blockstream Launches Institutional Consulting Services, Opens Lugano Office
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Blockstream Launches Institutional Consulting Services, Opens Lugano Office
Blockstream will offer its engineering expertise to banks and asset managers from a new Swiss base.
This post Blockstream Launches Institutional Consulting Services, Opens Lugano Office first appeared on Bi...
content:
Blockstream has launched a consulting business for financial institutions and opened an office in Lugano, Switzerland, the company shared today. The expansion gives banks, asset managers and other institutions direct access to the firm’s engineering teams and Bitcoin infrastructure, Blockstream said. 

Blockstream Consulting Services will support institutions through the evaluation, design and implementation of Bitcoin-based financial infrastructure. The company said the business will develop solutions for tokenized asset issuance, confidential settlement and related infrastructure, with services spanning technical strategy, system architecture, integration and implementation.

From Lugano, Blockstream plans to serve clients across Switzerland, including Zurich, Geneva and Zug. The company said the office will serve as a hub for its European operations, supporting client relationships, strategic partnerships and collaboration with the region’s financial and technology communities.

“Switzerland is an important market for Blockstream given its longstanding banking tradition and supportive regulatory framework for digital assets,” said Peter Bain, chief marketing officer of the company. “We look to provide regional expertise in markets where we see demand for Bitcoin infrastructure. Our consulting business, combined with our new office in Lugano, will bring tailored Bitcoin solutions to financial institutions across Europe.”

Founded in 2014, Blockstream develops technology and services across Bitcoin custody, settlement, payments, asset issuance and self-custody. Its products include the Liquid Network sidechain, Elements, Simplicity, Core Lightning, the Jade hardware wallet and the Blockstream App. This year, the company launched Simplicity smart contracts on Liquid and added Lightning support to Jade.

Bitcoin adoption by financial institutions

The company said the consulting business draws on that experience, with capabilities in cryptography, protocol engineering, security and financial technology. Multidisciplinary teams will give institutions access to the firm’s technical staff from initial evaluation through deployment.

“The next phase of Bitcoin adoption is its integration into existing financial systems,” said Adam Back, Blockstream’s co-founder and CEO. “Our extensive experience in Bitcoin cryptography, protocol development and engineering gives Blockstream the technical expertise to address the complexities of integrating Bitcoin into traditional financial infrastructure.”

The company framed the move as part of a long-term commitment to Switzerland and a broader strategy of building a presence in key markets to support institutional Bitcoin adoption. 

The country has become a center for digital asset firms, with Zug’s “Crypto Valley” and a regulatory framework that permits banks to hold and trade bitcoin on behalf of clients.

There was no pricing disclosed, headcount for the Lugano office or named clients for the consulting business. The company said the Lugano office is open and that consulting engagements are available to institutions across Europe.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: JPMorgan Brings Tokenized Money Funds to Solana for US Investors
summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management has expanded its tokenized money market funds MONY and JLTXX onto Solana, giving qualified U.S. investors access through the Morgan Money platform. J.P. Morgan Expands Access for Tokenized Funds J.P. Morgan is taking another step onto public blockchain rails. The asset m...
content:
J.P. Morgan Asset Management has expanded its tokenized money market funds MONY and JLTXX onto Solana, giving qualified U.S. investors access through the Morgan Money platform.

Key Takeaways

  • J.P. Morgan expanded MONY and JLTXX to Solana for qualified U.S. investors via Morgan Money.
  • Solana now has 19,789 tokenized credit holders and about 1.5M tokenized-stock holders.
  • Sustained balances and usage will show whether Wall Street tokenization is moving beyond launches.

J.P. Morgan Expands Access for Tokenized Funds

J.P. Morgan is taking another step onto public blockchain rails.

The asset manager has made MONY and JLTXX available on Solana through its Morgan Money platform, allowing qualified U.S. investors to manage subscriptions, redemptions, and token balances from a single interface. Both funds were previously available on Ethereum.

The expansion matters because it moves institutional cash-management products onto a blockchain better known for crypto trading, payments, and retail activity. It also strengthens the case that public networks are becoming part of mainstream financial infrastructure.

Solana Gets a Wall Street Cash-Management Product

MONY and JLTXX offer investors exposure to dollar-denominated money market strategies while using blockchain infrastructure for ownership and settlement.

For institutional clients, the appeal is less about speculation and more about moving traditional financial assets onto programmable rails.

The funds can also serve as reserve and cash-management tools for eligible stablecoin issuers operating under the U.S. GENIUS Act framework.

That makes the launch relevant not only to investors, but also to fintech companies and crypto firms building regulated dollar products. J.P. Morgan joins firms including Blackrock in testing how tokenized funds can operate across public blockchain networks.

Solana RWA Ownership Is Hitting New Highs

The timing is notable.

Data shared by Solana Sensei shows tokenized credit holders on Solana have reached a record 19,789, while holders of tokenized stocks across tracked markets climbed to roughly 1.5 million, up 6.7%. Among individual equities, NVDAx leads with about 190,100 holders, followed by SPCX at 111,100.

These figures suggest Solana’s RWA growth is spreading beyond total asset value into broader wallet-level distribution.

That distinction matters. Large institutional deposits can inflate tokenized asset totals quickly, but rising holder counts point to expanding participation.

Public Blockchains Move Deeper Into TradFi

J.P. Morgan’s move reinforces a larger shift in crypto.

Tokenization is no longer limited to experimental pilots or crypto-native issuers. Major asset managers are increasingly placing money market funds, stocks, and other traditional assets onto public chains.

For Solana, the opportunity is to become infrastructure not just for trading tokens, but for managing real financial assets.

The combination of J.P. Morgan’s arrival and record tokenized real-world asset holder counts gives the network a stronger institutional story.

The next test is whether these tokenized funds generate sustained balances and transaction activity rather than simply another high-profile launch.

title: Bitwise Dogecoin ETF Reaches Scheduled Liquidation As Holders Face Cash Redemption
summary: Bitwise’s BWOW Dogecoin ETF reached its announced October 22 liquidation distribution date, with remaining shareholders due cash based on the fund’s net asset value.
content:
TL;DR: Bitwise’s BWOW Dogecoin ETF reached its announced October 22 liquidation distribution date, with remaining shareholders due cash based on the fund’s net asset value.

For investors who held the Bitwise Dogecoin ETF past its final day of trading, the exit is now a cash-redemption process rather than a normal market order. The fund's previously announced liquidation calendar points to October 22 for distribution of proceeds to remaining holders.

Bitwise told investors in September that BWOW would cease trading on the NYSE Arca after October 14. The sponsor subsequently planned to liquidate the portfolio and distribute the value of remaining holdings through investors' brokerage accounts, using an October 21 net asset valuation.

What happens to shares after trading stops

An ETF closing is not the same as the cryptocurrency underlying its strategy disappearing. Dogecoin continues to trade in the broader market; the BWOW product is the investment vehicle being wound down.

Shareholders who sold before the final trading deadline exited through the exchange. Those still holding shares at liquidation are due cash based on the fund's applicable net asset value, subject to normal broker processing arrangements and the terms laid out in the regulatory filing.

The SEC filing says distributions are expected on or around October 22. That wording matters: a scheduled distribution is not proof that every brokerage account has already been credited by the time an article is published.

Bitwise described the closure as part of its decision to optimize the product range. That should not be turned into an unsupported claim about the specific reasons for every investor's decision to buy or sell the fund.

Why product closures deserve attention

Crypto investment products attract headlines when they launch, especially when a fund offers convenient exposure to a popular token. The exit process is less glamorous but equally important. A sponsor needs to manage trading cutoffs, portfolio liquidation, calculation of value and communication to holders.

A security can provide exposure to a digital asset without offering the same rights as directly holding coins in a wallet. Investors therefore need to understand how a redemption is processed and whether receiving cash may create a taxable event under their circumstances.

There are also lessons for issuers. New products compete for liquidity, attention and sufficient assets to justify their ongoing operating costs. The existence of an exchange listing does not guarantee a fund will remain open indefinitely.

This week's scheduled distribution provides a concrete reminder of that lifecycle. It is a corporate-action story about one ETF, not evidence that Dogecoin itself has undergone a protocol change or lost its entire market.

title: IRS plans lower tax disclosure penalties, including for crypto: Forbes
summary: The US tax agency is targeting faster resolutions and more flexible payment options for taxpayers voluntarily disclosing past tax violations under a planned program overhaul.
content:
The US Internal Revenue Service (IRS) is preparing to overhaul its voluntary disclosure program, with plans to reduce penalties and accelerate the resolution of tax violations, including those involving cryptocurrencies, according to a Friday report by Forbes.

IRS Criminal Investigation Chief Jarod Koopman said the agency aims to introduce the revised program before December, with a target of resolving cases within 120 days of taxpayers completing the required submission process.

The overhaul would reportedly not establish a separate disclosure process for digital assets. Koopman told attendees at the UCLA Extension Tax Controversy Conference that the IRS would handle digital assets through the same voluntary disclosure procedures used for other forms of tax noncompliance.

The IRS official also indicated that penalties under the revised program would be substantially lower than those currently imposed, although he did not provide specific figures. The agency is considering allowing taxpayers to settle outstanding liabilities through installment plans or offers in compromise.

The proposed changes would mark a shift from the existing process, which can take a year or longer to complete, according to Forbes. The IRS’s current voluntary disclosure program is intended for taxpayers whose willful failure to comply with tax laws could expose them to criminal prosecution, rather than those who made unintentional reporting errors.

Meanwhile, lawmakers are considering a separate voluntary disclosure program aimed at crypto taxpayers, including those who made unintentional reporting errors. Section 502 of the proposed Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act would establish a process for correcting past violations with defined penalties, unlike the IRS’s existing program, which primarily addresses willful tax noncompliance. The bill cleared the House Ways and Means Committee in September.

title: Swiss Regulator Approves First Domestic Spot Bitcoin ETF Under Fund Law
summary: Switzerland’s FINMA has authorized a Bitcoin ETF structured as a Swiss-law public investment fund; the approval differs from older exchange-traded crypto products already sold in Europe.
content:
TL;DR: Switzerland’s FINMA has authorized a Bitcoin ETF structured as a Swiss-law public investment fund; the approval differs from older exchange-traded crypto products already sold in Europe.

Switzerland has taken a significant step in how Bitcoin exposure can be packaged for ordinary investors. Financial regulator FINMA says it has approved the country's first publicly offered exchange-traded fund that invests directly in Bitcoin under Swiss investment-fund law.

The approval, disclosed October 20, concerns a Swiss-law collective investment vehicle categorized as an alternative investment fund carrying particular risks. It is not the first time Europeans have been able to buy a Bitcoin-linked exchange-traded product. The regulatory difference is the underlying fund structure and the protections attached to it.

Why the legal wrapper matters

Europe has hosted Bitcoin exchange-traded notes and other cryptocurrency securities for years. Some are debt instruments issued by a company, so the investor's legal claim differs from owning units in a regulated collective investment fund whose assets are held under a particular custody structure.

FINMA's announcement emphasizes safeguards around custody, operational risks and investor disclosures. The regulator says the asset manager and supervised institutions must take measures to reduce risks inherent in holding Bitcoin, alongside clear explanations of the fund's exposure.

The regulator has also allowed an exception to certain risk-diversification requirements, recognizing Bitcoin's long trading history and comparatively substantial liquidity among crypto assets. An exception is not a judgment that Bitcoin prices are stable; FINMA expressly warns that market risk remains very high.

The road from approval to trading

Approval permits the product to move toward market launch, but investors should check a particular fund's prospectus, trading venue, fees, redemption structure and custody arrangements before assuming it is equivalent to another Bitcoin vehicle.

For Swiss brokers and advisers, a locally authorized fund may fit more naturally into existing compliance and suitability processes than a foreign debt instrument. For asset managers, it opens a regulatory template that others can study when designing competing products.

The regulatory press release does not assert that buying the fund eliminates wallet or counterparty risk. Investors still face Bitcoin's price volatility, while intermediaries must manage the separate risks of fund administration, settlement and custody.

It is also worth resisting exaggerated claims about being 'Europe's first Bitcoin ETF' without qualification. FINMA's milestone is the first fund of this specified Swiss-law type, not the invention of European listed cryptocurrency exposure.

The long-term significance will depend on whether this new structure attracts meaningful assets, how closely it tracks Bitcoin and whether the prospectus protections translate into better outcomes during turbulent markets.

Source: www.finma.ch original announcement or data.

Related Reading: Bitcoin; crypto custody; crypto exchanges.

title: SEC Targets Tokenization, AI and Quantum Computing in 2027 Examination Priorities
summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is putting tokenized securities, artificial intelligence, and quantum computing under heightened scrutiny as the technologies increasingly reshape financial markets, according to its newly released fiscal year 2027 examination priorities. The SEC Targets ...
content:
The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is putting tokenized securities, artificial intelligence, and quantum computing under heightened scrutiny as the technologies increasingly reshape financial markets, according to its newly released fiscal year 2027 examination priorities.

Key Takeaways

  • The SEC named tokenized securities as an examination priority, focusing on clearing agencies and market infrastructure resilience.
  • Regulators will scrutinize AI-powered trading, investment advice, cybersecurity threats, deepfakes, and compliance systems.
  • The SEC flagged quantum computing as an emerging concern but stopped short of specifying risks to cryptocurrencies or mandating quantum-resistant safeguards.

The SEC Targets Tokenization in 2027

The SEC’s Division of Examinations identified the three technologies among emerging trends that will inform its oversight of regulated financial institutions, including clearing agencies, securities exchanges, broker-dealers, and investment advisers.

Tokenization, which involves representing traditional financial assets such as stocks and bonds as digital tokens on blockchain networks, appears in two separate sections of the report.

Under its clearing agency priorities, the SEC said examinations will focus on high-risk areas including default management, securities lending, operational controls, and tokenization. Clearing agencies play a critical role in processing and settling securities transactions, making their technological reliability essential to market stability.

The regulator also identified tokenized securities as an emerging concern under Regulation Systems Compliance and Integrity (SCI), which establishes operational resilience and technology safeguards for certain key market participants.

“Examinations under Regulation SCI will focus on emerging trends, including [AI], tokenization of securities, extended trading hours, and quantum computing,” the report states.

The references come as traditional financial institutions increasingly explore blockchain technology to modernize securities trading, settlement and asset management.

However, the SEC stopped short of outlining specific new requirements for tokenized assets, and notably did not establish separate examination priorities for cryptocurrencies, stablecoins, or decentralized finance.

AI Takes Center Stage

Artificial intelligence received substantially greater attention throughout the report, although the SEC repeatedly referred to the technology as “super intelligence,” or SI.

The regulator acknowledged that financial institutions are increasingly deploying advanced AI systems for investment analysis, portfolio management, customer communications, software development, and regulatory compliance.

“As these capabilities grow more sophisticated and embedded in daily business processes, the division is intensifying its efforts to understand how the technologies influence outcomes,” the report states.

The SEC also warned that malicious actors are exploiting advanced AI to launch increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks, including automated phishing campaigns and deepfake audio and video used to deceive employees and customers.

Examiners will assess whether financial institutions have adequately prepared for these threats and implemented safeguards against identity theft, account takeovers, and fraudulent transactions.

The agency also intends to scrutinize AI-powered trading algorithms and automated investment advice, particularly whether firms accurately describe their technologies and deliver recommendations consistent with investors’ financial objectives and risk profiles.

AI applications supporting fraud detection, anti-money laundering compliance, and back-office operations will also face examination. Meanwhile, the SEC said it is incorporating advanced AI into its own examination processes to improve efficiency, identify patterns and assess risks, while maintaining human oversight.

Quantum Computing Enters Regulatory Spotlight

Quantum computing also received explicit recognition as an emerging technology under Regulation SCI, although the SEC provided little detail about its specific concerns.

The inclusion is noteworthy as advances in quantum computing raise questions about the long-term security of cryptographic systems underpinning financial infrastructure.

For the cryptocurrency industry, sufficiently powerful quantum computers could eventually threaten the public-key cryptography used to secure Bitcoin and other blockchain networks, potentially necessitating upgrades to quantum-resistant alternatives.

The SEC did not directly connect quantum computing to cryptocurrency security or announce specific post-quantum requirements.

Beyond emerging technologies, the report emphasizes cybersecurity, third-party vendor oversight, investor protections, and coordination with other regulators, including the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC).

The document outlines examination priorities rather than new regulations, but its focus on tokenization, advanced AI, and quantum computing highlights the growing importance of technological resilience as traditional finance evolves.

title: Solayer Pay Adds Five Blockchain Networks For Direct Stablecoin Card Deposits
summary: Solayer Pay says its card app now accepts supported stablecoin deposits from Solana, Ethereum, Arbitrum, BNB Chain and Base without an additional bridging step.
content:
TL;DR: Solayer Pay says its card app now accepts supported stablecoin deposits from Solana, Ethereum, Arbitrum, BNB Chain and Base without an additional bridging step.

Moving stablecoins from a crypto wallet to a payment card has often involved an awkward detour through another blockchain or exchange. Solayer Pay is trying to remove that step by accepting deposits from five popular networks directly into its card balance.

In an announcement dated Thursday evening in the United States, Solayer said users can now fund the app from Solana, Ethereum, Arbitrum, BNB Chain and Base. The product supports deposits using eligible dollar-pegged tokens such as USDC and USDT on the supported chains.

The network problem behind a simple purchase

A dollar-backed token issued on one blockchain is not interchangeable at the technical level with a version on another network. A person might own USDT on BNB Chain while their payment app previously accepted deposits only on Solana. Bridging or exchanging the funds introduces extra steps, network fees and the possibility of using the wrong address.

Solayer says its new deposit flow lets users choose the network where their supported tokens already reside and credit a common Solayer Pay balance. Once deposited, that balance can be spent using virtual or physical cards where available, with the app also supporting compatible mobile wallets and peer-to-peer payments.

The company says more than 45,000 cardholders use the product. Solayer Pay was introduced as the Emerald Card in April 2025, with a physical card added later. Those are company-reported distribution metrics rather than independently audited payment volumes.

Spending is not the same as self-custody

The convenience comes with a change in the user's relationship to the assets. Once money is deposited into an app balance, customers need to understand which provider holds it, how withdrawals work and what rules apply if an account is restricted or a supported chain becomes congested.

Geographic eligibility and identity-verification requirements also matter. A Visa-linked card program's global acceptance network does not automatically mean that every person worldwide can obtain the card or deposit every stablecoin.

Still, the launch addresses a real weakness in current crypto payments: users are asked to understand blockchain routing before making ordinary purchases. Removing some of that complexity could be commercially useful even if the underlying payment ultimately settles through existing card networks.

The next question is whether stablecoin deposits translate into meaningful card use. That is a harder measure of adoption than the number of available networks or wallets.

title: Netanyahu Orders Blockchain Plan to Help Israel Evade Potential Sanctions
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has directed officials to prepare a plan involving blockchain technology and cryptocurrencies to help the country circumvent potential international economic sanctions, including restrictions on its banking system.   Israel Weighs Blockchain Solution Speakin...
content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has directed officials to prepare a plan involving blockchain technology and cryptocurrencies to help the country circumvent potential international economic sanctions, including restrictions on its banking system.

Key Takeaways

  • Israel’s prime minister has directed officials to explore cryptocurrencies and blockchain technology to circumvent potential international banking sanctions.
  • The initiative comes amid growing international pressure on Israel, with Netanyahu also calling for reduced reliance on U.S. military assistance.
  • Blockchain could facilitate cross-border transactions outside traditional banking channels, but transparency, regulatory restrictions, and liquidity constraints could limit its effectiveness in evading sanctions.

Israel Weighs Blockchain Solution

Speaking in an interview with Israel’s Channel 10 on Friday, Netanyahu acknowledged growing concerns about foreign economic pressure and said Israel must develop alternative financial mechanisms to reduce its vulnerability.

“We need to understand that there could be banking sanctions. You need to prepare an alternative economic system, and you know what that is, and you know which currencies can bypass this, and I’m working on that as well,” Netanyahu said, according to The Jerusalem Post.

When asked specifically whether blockchain technology could provide an alternative to conventional financial channels, Netanyahu confirmed that it was among the options being considered.

“One of them. Certainly. And I’ve already asked for a plan to be prepared for that,” he said.

The prime minister did not specify which cryptocurrencies or blockchain networks might be involved, which government agencies would oversee the initiative, or when such a system could be implemented.

The proposal raises the prospect of Israel turning to decentralized financial infrastructure to maintain international transactions if traditional banking channels become restricted.

Cryptocurrencies can facilitate cross-border transfers without relying directly on conventional banking networks, although their effectiveness in circumventing sanctions remains limited by exchange controls, liquidity requirements, blockchain surveillance, and restrictions on financial intermediaries.

Netanyahu’s remarks come amid mounting international criticism of Israeli government policies in Palestine and efforts by several countries to impose economic restrictions related to the country’s military operations and settlement activities.

According to a database maintained by the Jewish People Policy Institute, the United States accounts for 15 recorded measures targeting Israel, followed by Spain with 10, the United Kingdom with eight, Turkey with seven, and Belgium with five. The figures include a broad range of actions, including proposed legislative measures and institutional boycotts, rather than exclusively financial sanctions.

Netanyahu also warned that Israel should prepare for an eventual end to American military assistance, arguing that the country could no longer assume continued access to tens of billions of dollars in U.S. defense funding.

The comments suggest a broader effort to reduce Israel’s dependence on foreign financial and military support, with blockchain technology emerging as one possible component of that strategy.

title: CMCC Global Plans Tokenized Bitcoin Funds With Tether And Bitfinex Securities
summary: CMCC Global is bringing two existing fund strategies into tokenized securities issued through Tether’s Hadron infrastructure and Bitfinex Securities under El Salvador’s rules.
content:
TL;DR: CMCC Global is bringing two existing fund strategies into tokenized securities issued through Tether’s Hadron infrastructure and Bitfinex Securities under El Salvador’s rules.

The tokenization of financial products is moving beyond Treasury bills and cash-like instruments. Investment manager CMCC Global has announced plans to represent interests in two digital-asset funds as tokens through infrastructure supplied by Tether and a regulated securities venue operated by Bitfinex.

The funds are called Crest and the Liberty Bitcoin Accumulation Fund, or LBAF. CMCC describes the offerings as fund-of-funds structures under El Salvador's digital-asset framework, with issuance and token management on Hadron by Tether and distribution through Bitfinex Securities.

Two strategies, two ways to measure returns

Crest is denominated in U.S. dollars and aims to outperform Treasury-bill yields. LBAF instead measures performance in Bitcoin and advertises a target annualized net return of 8% to 12% in BTC terms. Those are investment objectives, not guaranteed payments to token holders.

That distinction is especially important for the Bitcoin-denominated vehicle. An investor could accumulate more BTC units under one strategy yet still see the U.S. dollar value of their investment fall if Bitcoin's market price declines. Strategy, currency of account and liquidity are separate risks.

CMCC says the proposed tokens represent economic interests in the underlying fund shares. The structure is designed so tokens are created against corresponding shares and destroyed upon redemption. It remains a managed investment product with legal and operational conditions, not a permissionless token whose ownership automatically entitles anyone to the underlying assets.

Regulated access rather than open circulation

The announcement describes identity checks, anti-money-laundering requirements and whitelisted addresses for eligible self-custody. Bitfinex Securities is expected to provide issuance, distribution and secondary trading facilities under the applicable framework.

An institutional investor, BTCS S.A., has agreed in principle to provide an anchor allocation described as a three-digit amount of Bitcoin, although the exact commitment has not been disclosed. That is materially different from a public disclosure that a specific number of coins has already been transferred into the fund.

The stated issue price is $10 per Crest token and 0.0001 BTC per LBAF token. Neither unit price should be confused with proof of portfolio returns or uninterrupted secondary-market liquidity.

If the offerings attract sustained investors, they could show how blockchain settlement fits into professionally managed crypto strategies without dismantling the familiar structure of a regulated fund. The first hurdle, however, is successful issuance and ongoing administration. Technology can make transfer records programmable; it cannot eliminate investment losses, valuation disputes or the need for transparent fund governance.

title: Initia halts blockchain after exploit reportedly drains over $2.6M
summary: The blockchain suspended its layer-1 network and rollups after security researchers identified unauthorized token minting and millions in assets transferred to Ethereum.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedOct 23, 2026

The blockchain suspended its layer-1 network and rollups after security researchers identified unauthorized token minting and millions in assets transferred to Ethereum.

Initia halted its layer-1 blockchain and rollups after blockchain sleuths reported an exploit that allowed an attacker to mint tokens without authorization and drain more than $2.6 million in crypto assets.

The network was halted at 3:41 p.m. UTC on Friday following a security incident, Initia said in a post on X. The team said it was working with security researchers, validators and exchanges to determine the full extent of the impact.

Blockchain security researcher Spreek first flagged the exploit on Friday, reporting that an attacker had minted tokens without authorization and converted approximately $2.6 million into other assets, with additional funds still being moved.

DeFi platform D2 Finance later reported that the attacker exploited a vulnerability to mint 2 million AUSD tokens without sufficient backing. The attacker then used cross-chain transfers to withdraw approximately 1.4 million AUSD, 105 Ether (ETH) and 1.08 million USDC (USDC) to Ethereum.

The stolen assets were subsequently consolidated into an Ethereum wallet holding approximately 1,135.5 ETH, worth $2.73 million, according to D2 Finance. The firm attributed the exploit to a vulnerability in a Move function that allowed the attacker to create unbacked tokens and exchange them for assets on Ethereum.

Source: Initia

Initia is a layer-1 blockchain designed to support a network of interconnected rollups, known as Minitias. Its native token, INIT, briefly fell to around $0.115 on Friday before rebounding above $0.15, according to CoinGecko data. The token was trading near $0.1496 at the time of writing, an increase of about 14% over the previous 24 hours.

Initia has not publicly confirmed the estimated losses or the precise cause of the exploit, and the extent of the impact on users and the timeline for restoring network operations remain unclear. Cointelegraph was unable to contact Initia for additional comment through its official X account.

title: HSBC Launches First Stablecoin, Bringing Hong Kong Dollar Payments to 3.3M Users
summary: HSBC has launched its first stablecoin, a Hong Kong dollar-backed digital currency designed for everyday payments, marking a significant step toward mainstream adoption of blockchain-based financial services in the city. HSBC Launches Hong Kong Stablecoin The banking giant announced Friday that HSBC...
content:
HSBC has launched its first stablecoin, a Hong Kong dollar-backed digital currency designed for everyday payments, marking a significant step toward mainstream adoption of blockchain-based financial services in the city.

Key Takeaways

  • HSBC launched RedCoin (RCHKD), a regulated Hong Kong dollar-backed stablecoin, through its PayMe platform, reaching 3.3 million users and over 100,000 merchants.
  • RedCoin enables instant payments and transfers, with plans to expand into HSBC’s banking app, tokenized investments, and institutional transactions.
  • The launch strengthens Hong Kong’s digital asset ambitions, building on HSBC’s existing blockchain initiatives, including tokenized bonds, gold, and deposits.

HSBC Launches Hong Kong Stablecoin

The banking giant announced Friday that HSBC RedCoin (RCHKD) is launching through its PayMe mobile payments platform, giving more than 3.3 million users access to the regulated stablecoin. Customers will be able to activate stablecoin wallets within the app over the coming days, enabling instant transfers to friends and family and payments at more than 100,000 merchants.

RedCoin is designed to maintain a one-to-one value with the Hong Kong dollar and is backed by highly liquid, segregated assets. HSBC received its stablecoin issuer license from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) in April under the city’s new regulatory framework.

The launch follows months of preparation, including pilot testing with nearly 100 HSBC employees who evaluated wallet activation, stablecoin issuance, and transfers.

“Money, assets, and information are moving from traditional infrastructure to always-on, data-rich and increasingly programmable digital networks,” said Maggie Ng, HSBC’s Hong Kong CEO. She said the bank sees an opportunity to help customers navigate that transition through practical financial products.

HSBC plans to expand RedCoin’s capabilities later this year by integrating stablecoin wallets into its HSBC HK Mobile Banking App. Customers will also be able to use the digital currency to purchase tokenized investment products, including a forthcoming share class of the bank’s Hong Kong dollar money market fund.

The bank also intends to expand RedCoin into wholesale corporate and institutional applications.

“This is only the beginning,” said John O’Neill, HSBC’s managing director of digital assets and currencies, describing the launch as a major step toward making regulated digital assets widely accessible in Hong Kong.

The stablecoin builds on HSBC’s broader blockchain initiatives, including its Orion digital bond issuance platform, which has facilitated more than $8.3 billion in digitally native bond issuances since 2023.

HSBC also offers a tokenized gold product that has generated $2.5 billion in trading volume across 390,000 transactions since its 2024 launch, along with tokenized deposit services for wholesale payments.

The RedCoin rollout comes as Hong Kong seeks to establish itself as a global digital asset hub through regulatory oversight and expanded institutional participation in blockchain-based finance.

title: US Senator Questions Tether Over Reported Payments Linked To Former Crypto Adviser
summary: Senator Richard Blumenthal has demanded records from Tether and consultancy Nxum over reported payments and potential ethics concerns; the inquiry is not a finding of wrongdoing.
content:
TL;DR: Senator Richard Blumenthal has demanded records from Tether and consultancy Nxum over reported payments and potential ethics concerns; the inquiry is not a finding of wrongdoing.

Tether is facing questions from a senior U.S. senator over reported payments to a consultancy connected to a former White House crypto-policy official. The concern is about potential conflicts of interest in policymaking, rather than the reserve backing or technical operation of USDT.

On Thursday, Senator Richard Blumenthal, the ranking member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, said he had sent letters seeking information from Tether and Nxum Group. The inquiry follows reporting that payments flowed to a firm associated with Bo Hines, who previously led the White House Council of Advisers for Digital Assets.

What the senator is seeking

Blumenthal's public letter cites Wall Street Journal reporting alleging that more than $6 million was paid to Nxum under an arrangement involving strategic communications and public affairs. The senator raises questions about the firm's ownership, lobbying contacts and the timing of policy discussions during Hines's government service.

Those allegations are attributed to the reporting and to the senator's interpretation of it. They are not judicial findings or proven violations of ethics law. The existence of an investigative letter alone does not establish that Tether, Hines or the consultancy acted unlawfully.

The senator has requested records on contracts, payments, communications and lobbying activity. That documentary evidence, and responses from the parties involved, would be central to establishing what actually happened.

The stakes extend beyond one stablecoin issuer

Stablecoin legislation has become a major policy issue because issuers of digital dollars increasingly intersect with banks, payment providers and federal financial regulators. Companies have legitimate reasons to explain their business models to government; public officials are separately subject to rules intended to protect decision-making from personal financial interests.

The difficulty lies in distinguishing ordinary policy advocacy from arrangements that create an impermissible conflict. Large payments to a consultancy and past connections to an official are facts worth examining only in the context of ownership, contractual services, relevant dates and actual conduct.

For holders of USDT, the inquiry does not itself imply any change to redemption terms or reserve assets. For the policy community, however, the questions could invite closer attention to lobbying disclosures and the role of advisers moving between government and the crypto sector.

The next material development would be a substantive response, additional records or a formal investigation producing findings. Until then, the responsible description is that a senator has opened an inquiry into reported transactions — not that wrongdoing has been established.

Source: www.blumenthal.senate.gov original announcement or data.

title: US senator probes Tether after reported deal with ex-Trump crypto adviser
summary: The Democratic ranking member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations asked Paolo Ardoino for records related to a reported deal between Tether and Nxum.
content:
Update (Oct. 23, 6:27 pm UTC): This article has been updated to include a response from Tether.

Senator Richard Blumenthal has requested information from Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino after a Wall Street Journal report said that the stablecoin issuer had inked a $6.3 million deal with a marketing company co-founded by former White House crypto adviser Bo Hines.

In a Thursday letter to Ardoino, the Connecticut lawmaker said that the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations demanded “records and information related to contracts, payments, communications, and lobbying” between Tether and Nxum, Hines’ company. The probe into Nxum, Tether and Hines, according to Blumental, was part of what the senator called the Trump administration’s “self-enrichment and self-dealings with cryptocurrency firms.”

“While Hines failed to divest his one-third stake in Nxum [...] he worked closely over encrypted messaging applications with Nxum to coordinate lobbying, advocacy, and browbeating of members of Congress that were opposed to, or had sought changes to, pending stablecoin legislation,” said Blumenthal. “Those messages also reportedly demonstrate that Tether was directly coordinating Nxum’s lobbying efforts on the GENIUS Act which would regulate stablecoins, with CEO Paolo Ardoino demanding that Nxum ‘obliterate’ the legislation’s opponents.”

The lawmaker added:

“The highly unusual terms and nature of Tether’s business relationship with both Nxum and Bo Hines raise alarming ethical and legal concerns, indicating that Tether was likely well aware of the illegality and impropriety of issuing payments to a current White House official with such a direct role in shaping cryptocurrency legislation that was instrumental to its business.”

Hines worked as executive director as President’s Council of Advisers on Digital Assets from January to August 2025, when he left the White House to join Tether as a “strategic adviser.” He later became CEO of Tether US. Harry Jung, another crypto adviser in the Trump administration, left his position in July 2026 and joined Nxum as a managing director in August.

A Tether spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the company was aware of the allegations and an external counsel ”found no evidence of wrongdoing” after a previous ”in-depth internal investigation into the matter.”

Related: Trump didn‘t mention ‘crypto’ once in White House cybercrime roundtable

Trump, his family and members of his administration continue to face scrutiny over accusations that they are reaping financial windfalls from crypto policies on laws over which they have control or influence. The president disclosed earning $1.4 billion from investments related to crypto in 2025.

Crypto ties could be a factor in midterm elections

While Blumenthal has limited authority as the Democratic ranking member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, the results of the 2026 midterm elections could potentially change party control in the House of Representatives and Senate. This could give the Connecticut lawmaker and other Democratic additional authority to conduct investigations into Trump and his administration’s ties to the crypto industry, including those which could present conflicts of interest.

As of Friday, event contracts on prediction market platforms Kalshi and Polymarket favored Democrats retaking majority control of both chambers of Congress in 2027, with 92% and 68% chances on Kalshi for the House and Senate, respectively. US Election Day is on Nov. 3.
