title: Live updates: Bitcoin holds above $81,000 as oil prices hit six-month high
summary: Brent crude oil surged above $116 per barrel for the first time since late April.
content:
coverage endedOct 23, 2026, 4:30 p.m. EDT

Brent crude oil surged above $116 per barrel for the first time since late April.

You are here: 'The bad part of October'

“This part of October is historically one of the worst of the year,” writes Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group.

“The good news is late October lows are quite normal and with sentiment getting extreme, we could be looking at another late October buying period.”

Detrick is writing about traditional equity markets, but to the extent that crypto markets are correlated, it’s worth considering.

Yields edge higher after yesterday's plunge

Yesterday’s 19 basis point slide in the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield was the largest one-day move downward since March 2023, when the failure of Silicon Valley Bank had investors worried about a domino effect across the country.

Markets having calmed for the moment — the Nasdaq and S&P 500 are about flat on Friday, and French bond spreads (to Germany) are little changed — yields are cautiously edging higher.

The U.S. 10-year yield is up 4.3 basis points to 4.994%, and the 2-year yield is up 6 basis points to 4.695%.

Next week brings the Federal Reserve’s policy meeting, and investors continue to overwhelmingly bet the central bank leaves its benchmark fed funds rate unchanged.

Gold trades below $4,000 an ounce

Gold fell below $4,000 an ounce for the first time since July, trading around $3,990, roughly 30% below its January all-time high of $5,600. Silver has dropped more than 2% over the past 24 hours to around $53.40 an ounce, leaving it 56% below its January record high.

World oil prices continue surge, hitting six-month high

Brent crude oil — typically considered the global benchmark — is now higher by 2.6% and above $116 per barrel for the first time since late April

WTI crude oil — the U.S. domestic benchmark, is ahead 3.1% to a one-month higher of $102.53.

U.S. stocks are modestly lower, the Nasdaq down 0.2% and the S&P 500 off 0.6%.

Bitcoin has turned lower too, dipping back to $81,000.

Final UMich October consumer sentiment tops estimates

The University of Michigan Index of Consumer Sentiment edged down to 48.0 in October from 48.1 a month earlier. That’s up, though, from the preliminary reading of 46.3 two weeks ago.

The Index of Consumer Expectations rose to 48.8 from 46.3.

One-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7% from 4.6%, but were flat from the 4.7% preliminary read.

Longer-run inflation expectations rose to 3.5% from 3.4%, also in line with the preliminary read.

Bloom Energy shares fall 10%

Good news is bad news as the AI trade continues to struggle. Bloom Energy (BE) shares fell 10% in U.S. trading on Friday despite beating revenue and earnings expectations on Thursday. Third-quarter revenue rose 138% year over year to $1.24 billion, exceeding forecasts of $1.07 billion, while adjusted earnings per share reached $0.94, ahead of the $0.67 expected.

Time in the market versus timing the market

Even with yesterday’s ugly action included, bitcoin BTC$84,459.46 has gained about 39% over the nearly four months since it sat just below $59,000 on July 1.

One trader crunched the numbers. Since July 1, there have been 2,724 hourly candles, and the 15 strongest candles — just 0.55% — produced enough gains for that entire 39% advance.

Removing the 20 strongest hours over the last four months, and bitcoin would have actually dropped 6.8%.

“This is exactly why going fully cash and waiting for the ‘perfect entry’ is so dangerous,” the trader concluded. “Bitcoin could spend weeks doing absolutely nothing and deliver the entire rally while you are waiting to buy lower.”

Bitcoin struggles below spot ETF cost basis of $82,313

Bitcoin continues to struggle below the average cost basis of U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs, trading just above $81,000 compared with $82,313.

The chart tracks the running average price at which bitcoin has flowed into these ETFs.

Bitcoin ETFs had largest outflows since June; history says outlook isn't good

The U.S.-listed spot bitcoin ETF suffered $635 million in outflows during yesterday’s panicky action, according to Farside Investors. That’s the largest daily outflow since June 25.

While the contrarian take might be, “fantastic, the leveraged, fast-money types were flushed out, and now we’re poised to move higher,” history suggests otherwise.

According to Farside, bitcoin has tended to perform poorly in the days and weeks following outsized outflows. For instances of outflows greater than $300 million (there have been 22 such days prior to yesterday), bitcoin, on average, was significantly lower 7, 30, and 90 days later.

The caveat, of course, is that history is quite limited, given the ETFs have been around for less than three years, and is also likely skewed by the bear market begun in October 2025.

Bitcoin goes quiet near $81,500 after a week of $3,000 swings

Bitcoin dipped to about $81,000 late Thursday and has since spent the day boxed in a range of less than $1,000, trading near $81,500 early Friday. After a week of $3,000 swings, it’s the calmest stretch bitcoin has had in days.

It’s down 0.4% over 24 hours and still sits below $82,500, the support it lost on Thursday.

Altcoins were mixed. BNB was the standout, up nearly 2% to about $745, and DOGE added about 1%. XMR gave back part of Thursday’s jump, falling 7% to about $607, and ZEC lost nearly 4% to about $1,200. HYPE, XRP, ether and SOL slipped about 1% or less, with ether just under $2,400, according to CoinDesk data.

Stocks found their footing too. Nasdaq 100 futures were little changed after the index’s worst day since June, and an ETF tracking chipmakers edged higher before the open. Meta kept falling, while SpaceX climbed on reports that it plans to become a wireless carrier.

Oil is the worry. Brent crude touched its highest level since early May, which complicates the inflation outlook heading into the Fed’s Oct. 27–28 meeting. Treasuries gave back some of Thursday’s haven rally, which had pushed the 10-year yield down by the most in more than a year. Gold and the dollar were flat.

title: Bitcoin steadies near $81,700 as altcoins rebound, pepe climbs 13%
summary: Bitcoin rose 0.5% to around $81,700 since midnight UTC while the CoinDesk 80 gained 1.4% and memecoins climbed 2.9%.
content:
Oct 23, 2026, 6:54 a.m. EDT

4 min read

Summary

  • Bitcoin rose 0.5% to around $81,700 since midnight UTC, recovering from a low of around $81,000, while Asian stocks steadied after Thursday’s tech sell-off.
  • Altcoins moved faster, with the CoinDesk 80 gaining 1.4%, memecoins climbing 2.9% and frog-themed memecoin pepe jumping 13%.
  • Traders are now looking to the Fed’s Oct. 27-28 meeting.

Bitcoin BTC$84,459.46 rose 0.5% to around $81,700 since midnight UTC, outpaced by altcoins. Ether ETH$2,490.55 rose 0.9% and the CoinDesk 80 (CD80) altcoin index added 0.7% while the memecoin gauge climbed 2.9%.

The rebound follows Thursday’s tech-led selloff, during which the Nasdaq Composite index fell 2.6% in its steepest decline since June. Asian markets steadied as South Korea’s Kospi added 0.3% and China’s CSI 300 rose 1.7% while Japan’s Nikkei 225 slipped 0.25%.

Traders now look to the Fed’s Oct. 27-28 meeting, with Brent crude near $113 keeping inflation worries alive, and to exchange-traded fund flows, after U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost $635 million on Thursday, according to SoSoValue data, following more than $1 billion of inflows over the first three days of the week.

Derivatives positioning

  • Crypto futures trading cools: Volume fell 19% over 24 hours and liquidations dropped 23%, a day after both jumped. Open interest (OI) rose 1% after declining yesterday, with bitcoin's price little changed, so traders are adding positions again, not just closing them. The long/short taker volume ratio tilts slightly to shorts, at 51.6% against 48.4%.
  • OI-adjusted CVD points to bullish reset: Cumulative volume delta (CVD) tracks whether market orders are mostly buys or sells. Yesterday most tokens ended the day below zero, with the weakest near -0.12%. Today, almost all are within 0.05% of zero. The exception is XAUT, sitting around -0.25%.
  • BTC and ETH, majors see quiet rebuilding: Futures open interest rose about 1% in both coins while their prices barely moved, indicating a modest build in new positions. Liquidations fell sharply, by about two-thirds in bitcoin and a third in ether. Bitcoin funding rose to 0.0067% from 0.0041%, so longs are paying a little more to hold. Ether funding is flat.
  • BNB and SUI, funding flips back to positive: Yesterday, shorts were paying longs in BNB and SUI, at -0.0048% and -0.0036%, and DOGE was steady. Today all three are positive, and funding rose in most of the top tokens. The prices of all three rose, so longs, not shorts, are now the ones paying to hold.
  • De-risking in mZEC, SOL, XRP and DOGE continues: Open interest fell in all four by more than price alone explains, so positions are really being closed. ZEC is the sharpest, with open interest sliding 8% on a 1.5% price drop. It is the second day of heavy exits, which points to capital flight.
  • New money keeps entering commodity perps: Open interest rose in gold, silver and crude oil for a second day. Gold and silver prices fell, and funding is positive in both, meaning that longs are the ones paying. Crude oil open interest rose along with a 1.4% price gain. Funding is negative, so shorts are the ones paying. The gold token XAUT looks different. It has the deepest negative OI-adjusted CVD of any token, meaning market sells dominated the action.
  • Monero's funding spike has faded: Funding for XMR was the hottest on the heatmap earlier in the 24-hour window. It has since cooled back to normal levels. The leverage build-up flagged earlier has eased.
  • Bitcoin activity sits in upside calls and ether activity in puts: In bitcoin, the most traded option was the Nov. 27 $98,000 call, followed by the Dec. 25 $88,000 call. Five of the most-active six are calls, all above the market, and the only put is a $76,000 contract expiring Oct. 30. In ether, puts take the top two spots, led by the Oct. 26 $2,200 put with roughly 9,000 contracts. The volume data doesn't say whether the trades were buys or sells.
  • 25-delta skew shows strong put bias in ether: Ether's one-week put-call skew is near 13%, so puts cost a lot more than calls, and it has climbed since early October. Bitcoin's one-week skew has dropped to about 4% from a mid-month peak near 14%. Bitcoin's downside worry has eased while ether's has grown, which fits the heavy put activity in ether.

Token talk

  • Pepe PEPE$0.0₅4654 rose 14% to lead the CD100, the biggest advance in a month. The jump extends the Ethereum-based frog memecoin’s gain to 23% over the week and 16% over the month, a run with no clear catalyst.
  • That performance sets it apart from the rest of the sector, where floki FLOKI$0.0₄2459, bonk BONK$0.0₅3069 and shiba inu (SHIB) rose between 3.3% and 4.9% today, but remain down as much as 16% on the month. Pepe’s 24-hour trading volume totaled around $353 million, 10% more than around the same time yesterday.
  • Layer-1 tokens polkadot DOT$1.1657 and cosmos ATOM$1.7685 both rose more than 5%, extending weekly gains to above 6%. Still, polkadot is still down 2.5% in October while cosmos is up 3.6%.
  • DeFi tokens bounced after leading Thursday’s declines, with uniswap (UNI) gaining 3.5% to around $7.25 and ethena (ENA) rising 2.0% to around 20 cents.
  • The CD100’s weakest monthly performers also rose, with doublezero 2Z$0.03202 up 2.5% and monad MON$0.02196 up 4.3%, though they remain down 49% and 31% over the month.
  • CoinMarketCap’s “Altcoin Season” indicator is at 58/100, rising from Monday’s low of 54/100 as positive sentiment continues to impact the altcoin sector during bitcoin’s tight trading range.

title: Born2trade CEO: “Everything is about gold now. Gold traders dictate industry standards and features”
summary:
Gold has lost about a quarter of its value since January, the Fed is hiking, and retail traders are more focused on the metal than ever. After 25 years in brokerage, here is what I think that means for traders and for the brokers who serve them.
Gold trades around $4,100–4,200 an ounce, roughly 24% ...
content:
Gold has lost about a quarter of its value since January, the Fed is hiking, and retail traders are more focused on the metal than ever. After 25 years in brokerage, here is what I think that means for traders and for the brokers who serve them.

Gold trades around $4,100–4,200 an ounce, roughly 24% below the record near $5,600 it set at the end of January, according to CIBC Capital Markets. The Federal Reserve is raising rates, not cutting them. By the old textbook, this should be a quiet time for gold.

However, it is not. In my more than 25 years in brokerage and trading, I have rarely seen retail clients this concentrated on one instrument. In our experience, and from what we see across the industry, between 70% and sometimes 90% of retail clients trade gold. That is a fact no broker can afford to ignore.

Why everyone trades gold

Nobody can give a precise answer to this, so I can only share how I see it. We live in a very complicated environment: geopolitical events, the war in Ukraine, uncertainty in the Middle East, and inflationary pressure that has kept building since COVID. Market participants — and simply people, are cautious about everything around them. Absolutely everything.

I read the total concentration on gold as a lack of trust in broader markets and investment instruments.

Gold stays the clearest asset for investors and traders, even though it is anything but clear when it comes to predicting its price.

The big money appears to agree. Central banks bought 345 tonnes of gold in the first half of 2026, according to World Gold Council data cited by CIBC, and gold-backed ETFs attracted a record $30.7 billion in the third quarter.

For brokers, the lesson is simple. The market and traders dictate what matters. A broker has to listen to its clients and build every development around their needs — not around its own dreams and ideas. That is how business works, and in 2026 the clients are telling us, very clearly, that they want gold.

Gold has no P/E ratio, and no obvious floor

Is gold expensive or cheap? From a classic valuation point of view, gold is much harder to judge than the S&P 500, the Nasdaq, or any asset with earnings, a P/E ratio, or similar measures. Honestly speaking, gold can cost $1,000–3,000, or $4,000–6,000 and higher. Naming a floor is far more complicated than for any equity index.

January showed how quickly sentiment can turn. Gold set a record of about $5,595 an ounce on 29 January. The next day it fell more than 9% — its sharpest one-day drop since 1983 — after Kevin Warsh was named as the next Fed Chair. By late June it had slipped below $4,000, roughly 29% off the high. And yet, compared with what markets are capable of, that crash was nothing.

So what is my estimate? I am convinced gold will stay one of the most actively traded assets through the end of 2026, and most likely through 2027. Over a one-year horizon, I see plenty of reasons for it to fluctuate anywhere between $3,000 and $6,000 if something truly unpredictable happens.

The forces on each side are clear. The Fed’s rate path and its fight with inflation — the Fed raised rates by 25 basis points in September, and the 10-year Treasury yield is above 5% — are calming bullish sentiment. Global risks, uncertainty, and central bank demand are helping the bulls. I expect this balance to continue for the next few quarters. For reference, CIBC now forecasts $4,500 for the fourth quarter and an average of $5,200 in 2027.

I watched Lehman collapse on my trading screen

What about stocks, indices, and AI? I see a lot of signs of a bubble, and similarities with the dot-com era and even the 2008 crisis.

I remember 2008 not from textbooks but from my monitor. I watched Lehman Brothers collapse through the trading platform. I watched the S&P and the Nasdaq fall while the Japanese yen rose in record steps in September that year.

The new wave of traders, many of whom have only known rising markets, needs to study this history, be aware of it, and be prepared. For many years, financial markets have mostly been in rise mode, with very short-lived corrections. That will not last forever, and traders must understand it.

There is another side to this. Being ready for big swings is good for active traders, because the biggest opportunities come in exactly those periods — together with the biggest risks.

What active gold traders demand from a broker

If I had to put it in one word, it would be flexibility. It starts with how clients deposit, runs through trading conditions and leverage, and ends with how they withdraw.

Money moving to a broker and out of a broker must be fast, even ultra-fast. Right now there is no faster or more flexible route than crypto deposits and withdrawals. Even open banking and cards are not that friendly for active traders and investors.

Trading conditions must be just as flexible. Active clients need to hold positions at low cost, react quickly, and sit more comfortably through turbulence. That is why brokers are now competing on the cost of holding gold overnight, on the choice of leverage and on loyalty schemes, not only on spreads. At Born2trade, for example, we have answered this with positive overnight swaps on long gold positions and a gold-linked loyalty programme. We also offer a separate low-commission, fast-execution account for traders who care most about speed. The direction is set by clients, not by us.

How to choose a broker in a turbulent market

In simple words, trade with a broker you feel comfortable with. That is the main criterion.

Regulation plays a growing role in that choice. Brokers regulated by Tier-1 and Tier-2 authorities are more and more often the first choice for clients, and for objective reasons: stronger investor protection, clearer rules, and more confidence in how client money is handled. That is a real competitive advantage, and clients see it. Still, regulation alone is not a 100% guarantee that a broker is fair, or that it fits you and your trading style.

Group reputation and openness to the public are key factors in judging how reliable your broker is. The company’s owners and top management should not be hidden. They should be open and reachable, and trading conditions should be clear and genuinely beneficial to clients.

More important than anything else, though, is one rule: the initiative to trade must come from the client.

It is great when a broker promotes good, competitive conditions — that is what competition is for. But there should be no promises of fast profits and no pushy sales at all. A solid, fair and legal broker will never push anyone, least of all a beginner, by calling constantly or pressuring them. The initiative must come from the trader, all the time.

Gold discipline and a clear mind

Gold will keep testing traders in both directions over the coming quarters. The brokers that win will be the ones that listen to those traders and build around what they actually need. The traders who win will be the ones who respect the risk as much as the opportunity.

My wish for every trader, and every gold trader in particular, is simple: gold discipline and a clear mind.

title: HSBC rolls out its first stablecoin to over 3 million everyday app users
summary: HSBC and Standard Chartered-led Anchorpoint received Hong Kong’s first stablecoin issuer licenses in April. Anchorpoint began rolling out HKDAP in August.
content:
Oct 23, 2026, 6:22 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • HSBC debuted RedCoin (RCHKD), its first stablecoin, on PayMe, letting more than 3.3 million users send money and pay at over 100,000 merchants.
  • HSBC and Standard Chartered-led Anchorpoint received Hong Kong’s first stablecoin issuer licenses in April. Anchorpoint began rolling out HKDAP in August.
  • The bank plans to bring RedCoin to its banking app later this year and let customers use it to buy tokenized investments, including a money market fund.

HSBC debuted its first stablecoin, RedCoin, a Hong Kong dollar token that’s being rolled out onto its PayMe app.

The token, which uses the ticker RCHKD, will let customers send money to friends and family and pay at more than 100,000 merchants. PayMe users, of which there are more than 3.3 million, will be able to activate a stablecoin wallet in the app over the coming days, according to the bank.

RedCoin gives HSBC a way to bring stablecoin payments into an app that customers already use. HSBC has said RedCoin will be fully backed by high-quality liquid assets held in separate accounts.

The rollout follows the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's decision to grant its first stablecoin issuer licenses in April to HSBC and Anchorpoint Financial, a Standard Chartered-led venture. Anchorpoint began a limited rollout of its HKDAP token in August, focused on institutional payments and settlement.

“Integrating stablecoins into platforms users already rely on removes the need for a separate wallet or exchange account, and lets people engage with digital assets as part of their existing payment habits,” Vincent Chok, CEO of FDUSD issuer First Digital, said in emailed comments to CoinDesk.

“Over time, that everyday exposure builds familiarity and confidence in stablecoins across the wider market,” Chok added.

HSBC plans to add a RedCoin wallet to its Hong Kong mobile banking app later this year, and is set to let customers use the token to subscribe to tokenized investment products, including a new share class of its existing Hong Kong dollar money market fund.

“We will soon add more products, including expanding into wholesale corporate and institutional use cases,” said John O’Neill, HSBC's managing director for digital assets and currencies.

title: Sweden’s central bank revives e-krona debate as stablecoins and digital euro loom
summary: The Riksbank sees an e-krona as critical to securing national payments and monetary control.
content:
Summary

  • Sweden’s central bank warns foreign stablecoins and a digital euro risk eroding krona demand.
  • The Riksbank sees an e-krona as critical to securing national payments and monetary control.
  • Lawmakers have yet to approve the e-krona, which would take at least five years to launch.

Sweden’s central bank is calling for lawmakers to reconsider a digital krona, warning that foreign-currency stablecoins and a planned digital euro could erode the currency’s role in payments.

An e-krona would give the public access to central bank money in digital form. A 2023 government inquiry found too little need for one, but the Riksbank says changes in how people pay and growing security risks may warrant a new review.

“If our cash becomes digital and Swedish kronor are not available in a usable digital form, then the krona may not be able to compete with other, more convenient digital payment instruments that can easily be used across borders,” Deputy Governor Per Jansson told Reuters on the sidelines of a conference.

The Riksbank hasn’t taken a position on issuing one, but wants lawmakers to start preparing legislation now, since the work would take at least five years.

The central bank warned that stablecoins tied to foreign currencies could reduce demand for the krona in a recent letter. It sees little near-term risk but says the long-term threat remains.

Cash use has fallen sharply in the country. Just 5% of Swedes surveyed used cash for their last purchase, according to Riksbank data cited in the report, and a shift away from the krona could make it harder for the bank to steer the economy and protect financial stability.

The Riksbank also sees an e-krona as a backup payment option during power or telecom outages, with offline payments among its potential features.

Sweden could draw on the digital euro’s infrastructure to build the system, with that central bank digital currency potentially debuting in 2029 if EU lawmakers approved the required rules.

title: What’s Really Going on Behind the Scenes of a Brokerage?
summary:
Trading technology has evolved considerably over the past decade. But has it evolved enough?
The January 2021 GameStop short squeeze was a watershed moment for the entire brokerage industry, making brokers brutally aware of how vulnerable their trading systems can be when activity peaks. 
Five years...
content:
2026-10-23T10:37:06.299+02:00

Friday, 23/10/2026 | 08:37 GMT by Finctra

Disclaimer

  • As geopolitics continues to drive market sentiment, trading activity is at its height. Brokers face the dilemma of widening their spreads to mitigate market risk or absorbing the cost of keeping spreads stable to satisfy traders.
  • Risk management technology provider Finctra begs to differ. According to a spokesperson, “Execution quality and margin protection should not be a trade-off. Brokers must have a clear picture of their exposure to reduce risk and prevent profit bleeding.”

Trading technology has evolved considerably over the past decade. But has it evolved enough?

The January 2021 GameStop short squeeze was a watershed moment for the entire brokerage industry, making brokers brutally aware of how vulnerable their trading systems can be when activity peaks.

Five years down the line, same story, different setting. Through predatory practices such as bonus abuse or cross-account arbitrage, traders continue to test brokerage systems, pushing them to the brink of collapse. Without clear visibility into such activities, brokers remain risk prone.

According to Finctra, the problem is “operational” and “systemic”. “To contain risk, brokers must still be able to identify it. Real-time visibility on potentially anomalous activity can help brokers spot intent before it becomes harmful," the spokesperson said.

The multiple facets of Finctra risk management

From an infrastructural perspective, many trading platform operators still run on disparate systems. From compliance to risk and trade reporting, every team uses different technologies. This leads to data fragmentation, with each team ending up with a fractured view of what happens on the other side of the trade. Finctra proposes a lucrative, system-driven solution.

Marketed as an institutional-grade risk management infrastructure, Finctra can help brokers continuously monitor and control risk while ensuring operational stability. Thanks to its multilevel capabilities, Finctra can monitor, detect, alert and respond to risk-threatening incidents in real time.

Built for MT4 and MT5 environments, Finctra’s technology suite can help streamline brokerage operations end-to-end, eliminating complexities from each core function, as follows:

  • RiskGuard helps monitor exposure and supports informed response in real time
  • Finctra Hub supports acumen by providing brokerage teams with a clear view of exposure and trading performance
  • OpsCenter equips MT4/MT5 admin and operations teams with the right tools to manage swap and tick data updates, handle batches or lots, and other recurring tasks hassle-free.

This layered platform architecture promotes a hierarchical yet unified view of brokerage operations in real time, qualifying Finctra as a brokerage risk intelligence partner for FX and CFD brokers. This is what makes it relevant across a variety of use cases.

Use case 1: Identifying margin risk

When volatility peaks, trading activity intensifies, increasing volume in specific instruments and amplifying brokerage exposure. Imagine the Fed changed its interest rate, surprising the markets to the upside. USD goes up against most of its major peers. Traders go long and short on most USD-based pairs and alternative assets, but one particular account holds multiple one-sided positions in EURUSD. This trader’s heavy exposure threatens to trigger margin call failures, generating negative balance risks.

Finctra’s RiskGuard can track this type of exposure in real time across individual accounts and multi-account clusters simultaneously. This flexibility allows teams to track both single large trades and the rapid accumulation of trading volume within short time windows.

Because a standard rule focused only on individual trade sizes might miss a high-volume threshold reached through multiple smaller trades, RiskGuard allows risk professionals to configure risk parameters based clear monitoring criteria, varying from individual large trades to volume accumulation over a short period of time. These parameters include trade sizes, specific time windows, order counts, and cumulative lots, all scoped to relevant account groups and symbols.

When a configured condition is met, RiskGuard automatically triggers an alert detailing the affected account, symbol, trade direction, specific trigger criteria, and timestamp. These data-driven, actionable insights help brokerage teams narrow down the possible activity triggers and formulate the appropriate response.

Use case 2: Understanding exposure and trading performance

To offer competitive pricing, brokers rely on multiple liquidity providers. During high-impact economic events like the NFP or central bank announcements, brokerage teams may notice concentrated exposure in specific symbols, such as XAUUSD or DJI. As traders respond to price spikes, the volume on these ticks increases drastically, with order books growing thinner by the hour.

The Finctra Hub addresses these challenges by providing a consolidated view on risk exposure and the overall trading activity carried out through the platform. By tracking multiple liquidity providers, Finctra enables appropriate position matching and facilitates reconciliation and trade reporting.

With a high-level overview of long and short positions, net exposure by symbol, and currency exposure analysis, dealers or risk managers can identify concentrations and review P&L and trading activity by trading account, symbol and country. This provides a solid basis for investigation, operational planning and decision-making.

The Country Analysis tool, for example, offers a unified view of country-level P&L, trading accounts and traded lots over a selected period. This level of detail enables teams to compare activities and results across different client markets and identify areas that warrant a closer look. Combined with broader trade intelligence, country-specific data informs regional planning and resource allocation.

The Hub’s functionality is enhanced by the Liquidity Connectivity and Infrastructure tools, which allow brokers to expand their liquidity pools across global venues while maintaining execution quality and stability. This level of flexibility enables risk professionals to streamline reporting, improve efficiency and acumen.

Use case 3: Simplifying platform administration

Market conditions change rapidly, and MT4 and MT5 brokers feel the pressure firsthand. To remain competitive and compliant, platform administrators must update swaps, apply configuration changes across multiple symbol groups, and ensure tick data is up-to-date.

These tasks can be time-consuming, and switching between different systems doesn’t make it more efficient. This is where the OpsCenter can make a difference. Designed to eliminate manual work and streamline processes for platform administrators, Finctra’s OpsCenter improves efficiency and reduces the risk of manual work-related errors in areas including:

  • Batch management & configuration: Instead of updating configurations symbol-by-symbol, platform admins can group assets by class, server and group type. OpsCenter allows users to select targeted symbol sets and apply configuration templates simultaneously.

  • Swap updates: Changing central bank policies affect currency prices and market liquidity, making swap rate updates necessary. The OpsCenter features swap update tools that enable swift batch swap updates for selected symbols, recording the values before and after each change, along with its success status, to enable straightforward review and tracking.

  • Tick data maintenance and downloads: To ensure optimal charting and backtesting capabilities for traders, platform admins must keep tick data fresh. Thanks to OpsCenter’s tools, platform administrators can maintain data accuracy through smooth and swift regular updates.

By removing manual work and the friction that comes with it from routine platform management, OpsCenter reduces operational risk, increases time efficiency, and ensures consistency across servers. This allows MT4 and MT5 admins to generate standardised templates for routine maintenance and focus more on system optimisation and platform stability.

The same standards of automation and flexibility spill over into reporting. Sitting alongside Finctra’s OpsCenter and RiskGuard, the Structured Reporting and Operational Visibility tools further enhance the risk management’s platform flexibility. By converting raw transaction and risk data into clear daily dashboards, the platform enables platform administrators to evaluate daily performance, track key risk metrics, and make informed strategic interventions with confidence.

A broker intelligence partner for brokers

As geopolitical headwinds and energy market volatility on one hand, and increasingly refined trading strategies continue to test brokerage systems, risk intelligence becomes imperative. Reliance on disparate systems creates dangerous vacuums that erode margins and generate systemic vulnerabilities over time. Finctra changes this paradigm, positioning itself as a risk intelligence partner for MT4 and MT5 brokers.

Building a cohesive layered infrastructure that brings together real-time exposure tracking and automated platform administration, Finctra eliminates operational complexities and reduces overheads. Doing so, it transforms brokerage management from a position of reactive damage control to proactive, data-driven operational optimisation.

Ultimately, Finctra proves that reliable margin protection and fast execution can and should coexist. In the long term, brokers that are able to act fast and eliminate toxic flow before it becomes harmful can also remain competitive.

Taking note of the valuable feedback and conversations at the event, the company looks into the future as it aims to take those discussions further and strengthen its connections. title: Ripple and Arf Bring $10B PayFi Settlement Liquidity to XRP Ledger With RLUSD
summary:
Key Takeaways: For licensed payment companies on the XRP Ledger, Arf is rolling out settlement financing using RLUSD. About $10 billion in settlement volume is processed annually and the financing
The post Ripple and Arf Bring $10B PayFi Settlement Liquidity to XRP Ledger With RLUSD appeared first o...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • For licensed payment companies on the XRP Ledger, Arf is rolling out settlement financing using RLUSD.
  • About $10 billion in settlement volume is processed annually and the financing is usually repaid within 1-5 days.
  • Once necessary changes are put forth, Arf expects to shift most of its activity to native lending on XRPL.

Ripple and Arf are building RLUSD to power short-term institutional credit, giving payment companies that need liquidity until a transaction is completed between countries a way to finance the process. The program aims to address a widespread challenge in global payments – enterprises frequently require liquidity in the destination market prior to receipt of funds.

  • RLUSD Becomes Working Capital for Global Payments
  • PayFi Links Credit Directly to Payment Flows
    • XRPL Native Lending Could Take the Program Onchain
    • XRP and RLUSD Play Different Roles

RLUSD Becomes Working Capital for Global Payments

Arf is making a settlement liquidity directly on XRPL in the form of Dollar Based stablecoin RLUSD. The financing will be for licensed payment, remittance and financial firms requiring short-term working capital to maintain cross-border transactions.

Arf says its existing business handles around $10 billion in annual global settlement volume. Its capital turns over about four times each month, reflecting the short duration of its financing model.

A settlement advance is paid back typically in 1-5 days after payments are made. This enables the same fund to be used over and over again and not tied up in long-term loans.

Read More: Ripple RLUSD Hits $2.5B, Enters Cross River Banking Stack for 24/7 Payme

PayFi Links Credit Directly to Payment Flows

Arf’s term for this model is ‘payment finance’, which he also refers to as PayFi. PayFi integrates lending, treasury management and foreign exchange into one single product to incorporate real-time payment flows.

This can cut down on balancing cash flows over a number of markets for cross-border businesses. Arf will take care of underwriting and working-capital as normal, while blockchain is responsible for settling and, ultimately, some aspects of the lending flow.

XRPL Native Lending Could Take the Program Onchain

The first phase does not require XRPL’s upcoming lending capabilities. Arf will issue credits to cover the settlement liquidity needs of the school district, initially through the existing committee infrastructure. The company also aims to shift more activity towards the proposed native lending platform for XRPL later on.

That’s a Single Asset Vault for onchain assets to aggregate funds, and a Lending Protocol to create structured loans out of that aggregation.

The specific ones, XLS-65 and XLS-66, must still complete XRPL’s amendment process for them to be enforced on mainnet. Arf states it has already developed within the proposed framework and will provide feedback for implementation in the future.

Read More: Ripple and Privy Bring XRP Wallets to XRPL After $1T Moved Across 8M Accounts

XRP and RLUSD Play Different Roles

RLUSD will be the collateral behind the loans and their repayments. Meanwhile, what is native to the network and will be needed for account and some ledger objects’ reserve requirements and transaction fees will still be XRP.

There may be a greater amount of recurring institutional activity on XRPL directly associated with actual payment flows, if settlement lending scales. The structure also allows payment companies to leverage Arf’s fiat and stablecoin treasury services without being present onchain while the blockchain layer is managed by XRPL.

title: Ripple Makes a Shock SEC Move After $150M XRP Lawsuit as OCC Unveils GENIUS Act Rules
summary: Ripple has endorsed the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission’s proposed cryptocurrency rules after spending more than $150 million on its legal battle with the agency.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XRP

Ripple has endorsed the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission’s proposed cryptocurrency rules after spending more than $150 million on its legal battle with the agency.

In an October 20 comment letter, Ripple supported the proposed framework while requesting changes to how federal securities law treats digital assets, investment contracts, and secondary-market transactions.

The development coincides with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) finalizing rules under the GENIUS Act, establishing federal standards for payment stablecoin issuers. Although the initiatives address different parts of the crypto industry, both could shape how digital asset businesses operate in the United States.

Key takeaways

  • Ripple backed the SEC’s proposed Regulation Crypto Assets on October 20 while seeking revisions to provisions affecting token sales and investment contracts.
  • Ripple Chief Legal Officer Stuart Alderoty cited more than $150 million in litigation costs, highlighting the financial burden of regulatory uncertainty.
  • The OCC finalized its GENIUS Act rule in October 2026, setting requirements for stablecoin reserves, redemptions, capital, and risk management.
  • The SEC proposal remains subject to rulemaking, while the OCC framework is scheduled to take effect on January 18, 2027.

Ripple Supports SEC Proposal After $150 Million Legal Fight

Ripple submitted its comment letter on October 20, the final day of the public comment period for the SEC’s proposed Regulation Crypto Assets. Introduced on August 18, the proposal seeks to establish a tailored framework for certain investment contracts involving cryptocurrencies.

Ripple’s legal team urged the SEC to distinguish crypto assets from investment contracts under the Howey test and replace case-by-case enforcement with clear regulatory standards. Source: @RippleXity via X

The company’s support marks a notable development following its years-long dispute with the SEC over XRP sales. Ripple is backing the agency’s effort to establish clearer rules but wants changes to ensure that securities law applies according to the terms of a particular investment arrangement, rather than automatically attaching to the underlying token.

Alderoty has argued that enforcement-driven regulation imposed substantial costs on the industry and pushed innovation overseas. Ripple’s reported $150 million in legal expenses illustrates the scale of its dispute with the agency.

The SEC proposal includes potential registration exemptions for qualifying offerings of up to $5 million over four years or $75 million within a 12-month period. Eligible issuers would remain subject to applicable disclosure requirements and federal anti-fraud protections.

It also proposes a conditional safe harbor addressing when an investment contract associated with a crypto asset may cease to qualify as a security. These provisions are not yet final, and their eventual scope will depend on the SEC’s consideration of public comments and its rulemaking authority.

Why Ripple Wants Clearer Rules for XRP Transactions

Ripple’s central concern is the application of the Howey test, the legal framework used to determine whether a transaction or arrangement qualifies as an investment contract under U.S. securities law.

The company argues that an investment contract involving a digital asset should not automatically make the token itself a security in every subsequent transaction. It wants the SEC to focus on the promises made to investors, the obligations assumed by the issuer, and the circumstances under which those obligations may end.

The post criticizes enforcement-driven regulation for pushing crypto innovation overseas and urges clear, Howey-based rules that distinguish investment contracts from the underlying tokens. Source: Stuart Alderoty via X

The issue featured prominently in Ripple’s legal dispute with the agency. In 2023, a federal court distinguished Ripple’s institutional XRP sales from certain programmatic sales on public exchanges. The ruling did not establish a blanket exemption for every XRP transaction.

The case reached a resolution in 2025, but questions about token classification and secondary-market transactions remain relevant to other cryptocurrency projects.

Ripple also challenges the use of decentralization as the decisive measure for determining when investment-contract obligations end. Instead, it favors standards based on the specific commitments and responsibilities associated with an offering.

The company’s position reflects a practical concern for crypto businesses: they need to understand which legal obligations apply when issuing tokens and when those assets subsequently change hands. The final SEC rules, if adopted, could help establish more consistent criteria.

Ripple’s $150 million figure refers to its reported legal costs, not the separate $125 million civil penalty associated with the case. The two amounts represent different aspects of the dispute.

What the SEC Proposal Could Mean for XRP

Ripple’s filing places XRP within a wider debate over how U.S. regulators should classify digital assets. However, supporting the SEC proposal does not change XRP’s legal status or guarantee that the agency will accept Ripple’s requested revisions.

Ripple’s support for the SEC’s proposed crypto rules marks a shift after years of litigation, following a 2023 court ruling that certain public-exchange XRP sales were not securities transactions. Source: The Wolf Of All Streets via X

If adopted with meaningful clarification, the rules could help businesses assess whether particular token offerings qualify for exemptions and when associated investment-contract obligations apply. Their impact would depend on the final text, eligibility conditions, and treatment of existing arrangements.

Other cryptocurrency projects, including Chainlink, Cardano, Hedera, Avalanche, and Stellar, have also called for greater certainty around token classification and the respective roles of the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

The debate has intensified amid setbacks for broader cryptocurrency market-structure legislation in Congress. SEC rulemaking provides another route to establishing detailed requirements, although it cannot resolve every issue that may require congressional action.

For XRP holders, the key development to watch is the final treatment of investment contracts and secondary-market transactions. Ripple’s comment letter is an attempt to influence those rules, not a guarantee of a particular outcome for XRP.

OCC Finalizes GENIUS Act Rules for Payment Stablecoins

Separately, the OCC finalized its rule implementing the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act in October 2026. Signed into law by President Donald Trump in July 2025, the legislation establishes a federal framework for payment stablecoins and generally restricts U.S. issuance to permitted issuers.

The OCC’s GENIUS Act rule tailors stablecoin issuer requirements and examination schedules to each entity’s business model, risk profile, size, and complexity. Source: @USOCC via X

The rule is scheduled to take effect on January 18, 2027, alongside the GENIUS Act. It covers national banks, federal savings associations, federal branches, and their subsidiaries, as well as certain nonbank and foreign issuers under OCC jurisdiction.

The framework sets standards for reserve assets, redemption rights, risk management, audits, reporting, custody, and capital safeguards. Payment stablecoins must be backed by qualifying reserve assets under the law, with requirements designed to support redemption and reduce risks to holders.

The OCC is also adopting a proportionate supervisory approach, tailoring examinations to factors such as an issuer’s business model, size, complexity, and risk profile. The framework is intended to maintain oversight while allowing eligible community banks to participate in the payment stablecoin market.

The GENIUS Act restricts stablecoin issuance to permitted entities while strengthening consumer protections and the dollar’s role in digital assets. Source: @USOCC via X

Additional reporting requirements will help supervisors monitor issuers’ financial condition and compliance. The OCC has developed weekly and quarterly reporting forms, which remain subject to applicable information-collection approval requirements.

Anti-money-laundering and sanctions requirements are being addressed through separate regulatory processes involving the relevant federal authorities.

The OCC framework does not determine whether XRP is a security, and Ripple’s SEC submission does not alter the GENIUS Act’s stablecoin requirements. The developments nevertheless highlight two parallel regulatory priorities: defining securities-law obligations for crypto assets and establishing safeguards for payment stablecoins.

The next milestones are the SEC’s review of comments on Regulation Crypto Assets and the GENIUS Act framework’s implementation in January 2027. Their eventual effects will depend on the final securities rules, the scope of the OCC’s requirements, and how the respective agencies enforce them.

Marc Ryan is Co-Founder and CEO of Spout Finance, a Solana lending protocol that lets people borrow USDC against tokenized US stocks without paying interest. Based in New York, Marc first got into crypto during the 2017 ICO boom and stayed through DeFi summer and the NFT cycle. Meanwhile he worked as a technology investment banker at HSBC, covering fintech, software and hardware, and that experience showed him how cheaply wealthy clients could borrow against their portfolios compared with everyone else.

Why you should listen

Spout starts from an argument about who tokenized stocks are really for. Marc points out that anyone with meaningful capital, almost anywhere in the world, can already open an Interactive Brokers account and buy US equities, so putting shares on a blockchain is not much of a breakthrough by itself. The more interesting question is what onchain stocks can do that brokerage stocks can’t. His answer is a lending pool that works like Aave or Kamino, with one structural difference. Instead of charging borrowers interest, Spout sells covered calls on their collateral every week, set well above the current price, and uses the premiums to pay lenders. Borrowers can take out up to half the value of their tokenized shares in USDC. The cost shows up as a small cap on their upside, which Marc estimates averages under half a percent a year, compared with margin rates of roughly 4.5% at the cheap end and 20% or more at some emerging-market brokers. Lenders, meanwhile, earn premium income that doesn’t depend on whether the stock goes up or down.

The conversation also covers how a small startup positions itself in a sector that is now attracting major institutions. Marc says most of the investors in Spout’s recent $2 million round were chosen for what they bring beyond money. Anchorage Digital provides the institutional custody that large funds require, Solana is the chain he considers best suited for bringing retail onto financial assets, and former CFTC Chairman Chris Giancarlo advises on navigating US regulation. Marc also explains why Spout gave up issuing its own tokenized shares. Running issuance alongside a lending protocol created too much legal and corporate overhead, so the team chose to be a permissionless layer that works with every issuer instead of competing with them. Most of those issuers wrap shares held with a custodian such as Alpaca. Marc contrasts that with native issuance from firms like Securitize and Superstate, where the shares themselves live onchain and can be self-custodied.

That distinction frames his view of the current regulatory fight. After a batch of companies objected to having their shares tokenized on OKXICE, the joint venture between OKX and NYSE owner ICE, under the SEC’s new Innovation Exemption, Marc argues that wrappers will keep serving offshore investors. US access, in his view, will come through native issuance or closer work with the DTCC. He is candid that a Spout token is undecided. If one launches, it would boost lender rates and allow options to be sold further out of the money. In the hot take round, Marc places himself between Bitcoin maximalism and multi-chain opportunism. He says every public equity will eventually move onchain, describes how AI agents now run parts of his own business, and names Back to the Future as his favorite film.

title: Tesla’s $TSLA Stock Token Lands on Solana Across 10+ Apps via Backpack Securities
summary:
Key Takeaways: Tesla’s $TSLA tokenized stock has debuted on the Solana network via Sunrise, while the issuer is listed as Backpack Securities. The token can be accessed via +10 Solana
The post Tesla’s $TSLA Stock Token Lands on Solana Across 10+ Apps via Backpack Securities appeared first on CryptoN...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Tesla’s $TSLA tokenized stock has debuted on the Solana network via Sunrise, while the issuer is listed as Backpack Securities.
  • The token can be accessed via +10 Solana applications: Phantom, Jupiter, Raydium, Kamino.
  • The launch opens the door to a novel method of tokenizing assets, bringing mainstream capital investment into the blockchain trading system.

Tesla stock has reached another side of the crypto market, and now a tokenized $TSLA exists on Solana. The launch will allow users to begin trading the asset in more than just brokerage apps, bringing tokenized equities beyond the walls of just brokerage platforms.

  • Tesla’s $TSLA Token Arrives on Solana
  • Ten Solana Apps Add Support for $TSLA
    • Wallet Access Meets Onchain Trading
    • Tokenized Stocks Expand Solana’s Crypto Market

Tesla’s $TSLA Token Arrives on Solana

Solana announced the launch on X, confirming that $TSLA is available through Sunrise and issued by Backpack Securities. The announcement also directed users to the Solana token directory to verify the asset’s contract address.

BREAKING: $TSLA is live on Solana via @sunrise, issued by @Backpack Securities https://t.co/VI8bODrEP7

— Solana (@solana) October 20, 2026

It is for this reason that it must be noted that it is a tokenized vehicle of Tesla stock, and not a token directly offered by Tesla.

In addition to its electric car efforts, Tesla is known for its energy storage solutions and autonomous driving and robotics technology. It is a popular and well-known name among investors and is a well-known stock on platforms looking to connect the blockchain to traditional financial assets. The companies agree to bring $TSLA exposure to Solana via crypto-native applications.

Read More: Securitize Puts 12 U.S. Stocks on Solana With 1:1 Backing and 24/7 Trading Plans

Ten Solana Apps Add Support for $TSLA

The list of platforms was given in the announcement where users can get the token. They include Phantom, Jupiter Exchange, Raydium, Titan Exchange, Fomo, dFlow, Archer Exchange, Meteora, Kamino Swap, and Mayan.

Wallet Access Meets Onchain Trading

This distribution has involved embedding the token in various aspects of the Solana ecosystem, including wallets and decentralized trading platforms. Access to the asset is provided via supported applications and not necessarily through a dedicated application.

But not all platforms have the same trading environment. Some venues can have liquidity, execution prices, fees, and access restrictions variations. Users must verify the market and confirm the token address prior to transacting.

According to the official announcement of Solana, the contract is called TSLAqBbv4CNCnzWFeB7LmydAyEiNMJtve7DYKLpdK4S. Confirms the entire address as there may be multiple unrelated tokens with the same ticker.

Tokenized Stocks Expand Solana’s Crypto Market

This launch brings another financial asset that is traditional to its portfolios to Solana’s expanding suite of blockchain solutions. Through tokenization, financial instruments and crypto wallets and onchain applications could become more easily foreseen in digital asset markets.

Tokenized equities also can help crypto exchange platforms appeal to customers who aren’t blockchain fans but have an interest in traditional asset categories. But their utility relies on legal rights that are associated with each token, arrangements, liquidity, and rules that determine eligible investors.

The $TSLA token is now available and will be trading on a much broader range of Solana applications. The future growth of adoption will depend on the success of trading, accessing users, and the value the token provides after its launch.

title: Barclays Plans 5,000 Job Cuts by 2026 in AI Efficiency Drive Despite £2.3B Profit and £500M Share Buyback
summary: Barclays plans to cut approximately 5,000 jobs by the end of 2026 as the British banking group expands its use of artificial intelligence (AI) to reduce costs and improve operational efficiency.
content:
Skip to content

Barclays plans to cut approximately 5,000 jobs by the end of 2026 as the British banking group expands its use of artificial intelligence (AI) to reduce costs and improve operational efficiency.

The planned reductions represent around 5% of Barclays’ global workforce, despite the bank reporting higher quarterly profits and announcing a £500 million share buyback.

Around 1,000 positions have already been eliminated, with most cuts targeting UK operational and support functions, including software development roles. The announcement comes as Barclays reports stronger equities trading revenue, while rising costs and regulatory concerns remain among the challenges facing the bank.

Barclays Targets 5,000 Jobs in AI-Driven Restructuring

Barclays described the initiative in its earnings presentation as “organisational simplification and technology change efficiency driven by AI.” The programme aims to streamline operations and improve productivity by integrating AI into existing business processes.

Sky News reports that Barclays plans to cut 5,000 jobs, around 5% of its workforce, as it invests in AI to streamline back-office operations, reduce costs, and improve efficiency. Source: @SkyNews via X

Approximately 60% of the planned job losses will affect support functions, including technology and software development teams. AI tools can automate routine tasks and assist employees with coding and other operational work, potentially reducing the staffing required for certain activities.

Most reductions are expected to affect operational and functional roles in the UK. With around 1,000 positions already eliminated, Barclays plans to complete the remaining cuts by the end of 2026.

Barclays Reports £2.3 Billion Quarterly Profit

The job-cut announcement coincided with Barclays’ third-quarter financial results. The bank reported approximately £2.3 billion in profit before tax, up around 12% year over year.

Profit after tax increased to £1.65 billion from £1.46 billion in the same period a year earlier, representing growth of approximately 13%. Total group income rose 3% to £7.37 billion, supported by stronger performance in its investment banking division.

Barclays posted £2.3 billion in Q3 profit, up 12% year-over-year, and launched a £500 million buyback, signaling efficiency-driven cuts rather than financial distress. Source: @Elizacreatez via X

Equities trading was a key contributor, with revenue from the business increasing 47% year-over-year.

Chief executive C. S. Venkatakrishnan highlighted the bank’s continuing operational and financial performance, pointing to strong results from the investment bank’s equities business.

However, higher profits have not eliminated concerns about costs and performance relative to market expectations. The results show that Barclays is pursuing workforce reductions while remaining profitable, rather than responding solely to immediate financial distress.

£500 Million Share Buyback Adds to Shareholder Returns

Barclays also announced a £500 million share buyback, through which the bank will repurchase its own shares. Buybacks return capital to shareholders and can increase earnings per share by reducing the number of shares outstanding.

The restructuring carries reported costs of approximately £501 million, reflecting expenses associated with implementing organizational changes. Although these costs can weigh on short-term results, lower payroll expenses could reduce operating costs over time if the planned efficiencies materialize.

The simultaneous announcement of job cuts and a share buyback has drawn attention to Barclays’ approach to cost management and shareholder returns. However, the available figures do not establish that the buyback is being funded directly by workforce reductions.

Barclays CEO Frames AI as an Enhancement to Existing Technology

Venkatakrishnan previously described AI as “the icing on the cake, not the cake” in a September interview with Bloomberg, emphasizing its role within the bank’s broader technology infrastructure.

Barclays CEO C.S. Venkatakrishnan called AI “the icing on the cake, not the cake,” with 1,000 roles already cut and remaining reductions targeted by year-end. Source: @vig_says via X

Barclays is incorporating AI into existing processes rather than presenting it as a wholesale replacement for its technology systems. Potential applications include software development, document processing, and data analysis, where automation can reduce manual workloads.

The planned reductions in support and development roles illustrate how AI adoption is affecting technical as well as administrative work. Banks must still maintain skilled teams to oversee automated systems, protect sensitive data, and meet regulatory requirements.

Costs and Regulatory Concerns Remain in Focus

AJ Bell investment director Russ Mould said Barclays’ third-quarter performance had fallen short of market expectations, adding that the share buyback had not fully eased investor disappointment.

Mould also pointed to rising group costs and two concerns for shareholders: a potential increase in taxes on the UK banking sector in the government’s upcoming budget and a reported investigation into possible misrepresentation of risks in the bank’s private credit portfolio.

Both issues could affect investor sentiment and the bank’s financial outlook. Any impact from taxation or the reported investigation will depend on subsequent policy decisions and the outcome of the relevant proceedings.

AI-Driven Job Cuts Signal a Shift in Banking Operations

Barclays’ restructuring reflects the growing use of AI to streamline operations across financial services. Banks are exploring automation to improve productivity and manage expenses, with software development and back-office work increasingly among the areas affected.

For Barclays, the key test will be whether the changes deliver lasting cost savings while preserving the technical expertise and oversight needed to operate a large financial institution. The bank has until the end of 2026 to complete the planned workforce reductions.

The announcement also highlights the employment implications of AI adoption. As banks integrate automation into routine workflows, the technology is reshaping staffing requirements even at profitable institutions. The longer-term effects will depend on how effectively companies translate productivity gains into sustainable operational improvements.

title: Travala Introduces AVA Buyback Multiplier, Scaling Buybacks Up to 4x Member Rewards
summary: Singapore, Singapore, 22nd October 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Singapore, Singapore, 22nd October 2026, Chainwire

Singapore, Singapore, October 22nd, 2026, Chainwire

Travala’s monthly AVA Strategic Reserve buyback will now match up to 3x the AVA rewards earned by AVA Smart members

Travala, the Binance-backed crypto travel booking platform, and the AVA Foundation—Travala’s loyalty program provider and issuer of the platform’s native AVA token—today announced the AVA Buyback Multiplier, an upgrade to the AVA Strategic Reserve launched in September 2026. 

Under the new structure, Travala’s monthly match of the AVA Foundation’s buyback scales with the AVA giveback rewards earned by AVA Smart members for booking travel, rising from 1x to up to 3x and taking total monthly buybacks to up to four times member givebacks.

Each month, the AVA Foundation buys back the AVA given to AVA Smart members as booking rewards in the previous month and returns it to its rewards pool. To date, the AVA Foundation has bought back 5,423,181 AVA through its monthly buybacks. Travala matches the monthly amount and moves it into the AVA Strategic Reserve, a multi-signature wallet Travala has committed never to sell or transfer from. Since the AVA Strategic Reserve launched in September, Travala has matched two monthly buybacks, and the reserve now holds 598,458.78 AVA.

Under the AVA Buyback Multiplier, the previous month’s AVA givebacks set Travala’s matched AVA buyback amount. Below $100,000 in monthly AVA givebacks, Travala matches 1x. The match rises to 1.5x at $100,000, 2x at $150,000, 2.5x at $200,000, and a maximum of 3x at $250,000 and above. This brings potential total monthly AVA buybacks to four times monthly AVA Smart member givebacks.

If monthly AVA givebacks fall below a target, the match returns to the lower level the following month. All AVA buybacks by Travala and the AVA Foundation are reported monthly and are verifiable on-chain.

“The AVA Buyback Multiplier ties AVA even more closely to our members’ travel bookings,” said Steve Hipwell, Lead Ecosystem Contributor at AVA Foundation. “Every booking that earns AVA giveback rewards now counts towards the next step up, and every token Travala buys back is permanently locked away in the AVA Strategic Reserve multi-signature custody wallet.”

“We want AVA’s tokenomics to be simple, transparent, and built around real activity,” he continued. “The Buyback Multiplier gives the Smart member community clear milestones to work towards, with every step published on-chain.”

The Buyback Multiplier follows the AVA Smart Program lock update and the launch of the Travala AI Agent on BNB Chain announced earlier this month.

About Travala

Travala founded in 2017 and now backed by industry giant Binance, is the leading crypto-native travel booking service, offering 2,200,000+ properties across 230 countries, 600+ airlines, 50,000+ car rental locations, and 400,000+ activities globally. Travala is a champion of cryptocurrency adoption, accepting over 100 leading cryptocurrencies alongside traditional payment methods. For more information, visit: www.travala.com.

About the AVA Foundation

The AVA Foundation oversees the AVA token ecosystem, including the AVA Smart Program, AVA token, and Travel Tiger NFTs. The AVA token functions as the key to accessing the AVA Smart Program, which provides travel perks and other benefits to Travala customers, such as AVA payment discounts and AVA loyalty rewards. AVA tokenises the concept of loyalty reward programs using blockchain technology, bringing web3 to traditional loyalty models. For more information, visit: www.avafoundation.org. 

Disclaimer

Travala may modify, suspend or discontinue the AVA Buyback Multiplier and future monthly purchases at any time. AVA already in the AVA Strategic Reserve remains subject to the never-sell commitment. This announcement is for information only and does not constitute financial advice, an offer to buy or sell any digital asset, or an inducement to acquire, hold or lock AVA. References to Travala are to TravelFront and its group companies. This announcement is not directed at persons in the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates or any jurisdictions where distribution would be unlawful.

title: Pudgy Penguins (PENGU) Price Prediction: Bullish SuperTrend Flip Signals Potential 70% Rally to $0.013
summary: Pudgy Penguins (PENGU) is showing a fresh bullish signal on its 12-hour chart, drawing attention to a possible recovery toward $0.013.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: PENGU

Pudgy Penguins (PENGU) is showing a fresh bullish signal on its 12-hour chart, drawing attention to a possible recovery toward $0.013.

The technical setup comes as PENGU trades near $0.0081 and approaches a key breakout zone.

Crypto analyst Ali Charts highlighted a bullish SuperTrend flip, noting that previous changes in the indicator’s direction had coincided with rallies and corrections. However, the signal does not guarantee another advance, and PENGU must overcome several resistance levels before a sustained recovery can be confirmed.

PENGU SuperTrend Flip Raises Bullish Price Prediction

Ali Charts identified the bullish SuperTrend signal as PENGU moved above $0.0081. The indicator is commonly used to assess market direction by comparing price action with a volatility-based trend line. A bullish flip can indicate improving momentum, while a bearish flip may signal weakening price conditions.

PENGU’s 12-hour chart shows a bullish SuperTrend flip above $0.0081, signaling potential upside based on the indicator’s historical trend-reversal signals. Source: @alicharts via X

The analyst also referred to an earlier TD Sequential analysis that identified buy signals preceding gains of 77% and 67%. A previous sell signal was followed by a 32% decline according to the post. These historical moves provide context for the latest signal, but they do not establish that PENGU will repeat the same performance.

Based on the possibility of another rally of roughly 70%, the analyst pointed to $0.013 as a potential upside target. From a price near $0.0081, that level would represent an increase of approximately 60%, rather than a full 70% gain. A 70% advance from $0.0081 would put the token near $0.0138.

The distinction matters because technical targets depend on the precise entry price and the size of the projected move. Traders will also need to monitor trading volume, resistance, and broader cryptocurrency market conditions to assess whether the bullish signal is gaining strength.

Symmetrical Triangle Puts PENGU Breakout in Focus

A separate TradingView analysis by CryptoNuclear identifies a tightening symmetrical triangle on PENGU’s four-day chart. The pattern has developed as the token records lower highs while maintaining progressively higher lows, narrowing the range in which it trades.

PENGU has formed a symmetrical triangle since peaking near $0.0466, with lower highs and rising support compressing the price range toward a potential breakout. Source: CryptoNuclear on TradingView

The structure reflects a market in which sellers continue to limit upward moves, while buyers attempt to defend higher support levels. As the two trend lines converge, the token approaches a point where a decisive move may become more likely. The pattern alone, however, does not indicate which direction the breakout will take.

PENGU previously reached a peak near $0.0466 before entering a prolonged decline and consolidation phase. With the token trading around $0.0081 in the supplied chart analysis, a recovery would need to overcome several overhead resistance zones to demonstrate that buying pressure is returning.

CryptoNuclear’s analysis emphasizes confirmation rather than anticipation. A sustained move above descending resistance, supported by stronger trading volume and a successful retest, would provide better evidence of a bullish breakout. A brief move above the trend line without follow-through could instead prove to be a false breakout.

PENGU Price Prediction: Key Resistance Levels and Bullish Targets

The four-day chart identifies $0.0105 as the first resistance level to watch. A move above this threshold could strengthen the recovery setup, although PENGU would still face additional barriers before reaching the $0.013 area highlighted by Ali Charts.

PENGU’s daily chart flashes a TD Sequential buy signal after previous signals preceded gains of 77.64% and 66.94%. Source: Ali Martinez via X

The next resistance levels are $0.0127 and $0.0150. The former sits close to the projected $0.013 target, making it an important level for evaluating whether bullish momentum can persist. A sustained break above $0.0150 would offer further evidence that the recovery is extending beyond an initial rebound.

If the token clears these intermediate barriers, the chart identifies $0.0232 and $0.0268 as more distant potential targets. Those levels would require a substantially larger advance and should be treated as conditional scenarios rather than near-term expectations.

The following levels summarize the main areas identified in the supplied technical analyses:

  • Initial resistance: $0.0105
  • Intermediate resistance: $0.0127
  • Key recovery threshold: $0.0150
  • Higher resistance zone: $0.0232
  • Extended bullish target: $0.0268
  • SuperTrend signal reference price: $0.0081
  • Potential support: $0.0065
  • Lower support zone: $0.0050–0.0037

These levels are based on the supplied chart analyses and may change as price action develops. They are not guaranteed points of reversal or continuation.

PENGU Price Prediction: Higher Highs and Higher Lows Support Recovery Case

Another technical analysis shared by @0xSweep points to a sequence of higher highs and higher lows on PENGU’s daily chart. This pattern can indicate that buyers are gradually gaining control, provided the token continues to defend its recent swing lows.

$PENGU is forming higher highs and higher lows on its daily chart, forecasting a potential 20%+ rally if Bitcoin holds above $83K. Source: @0xSweep via X

The analyst suggested that PENGU could gain more than 20% if Bitcoin holds above $83,000. Such a move would depend on both the token’s chart structure and conditions across the broader cryptocurrency market. Bitcoin weakness could undermine the setup by reducing risk appetite for smaller crypto assets.

Higher highs and higher lows are useful measures of price structure, but they do not confirm that an uptrend will continue indefinitely. A break below a previous higher low would weaken the bullish interpretation, while a move above a recent swing high could strengthen it.

The chart shows prolonged sideways consolidation after the latest down-wave failed to trigger a new up-wave, leaving the market awaiting a decisive breakout or breakdown. Source: MasterAnanda on TradingView

The longer-term outlook remains less certain. A separate TradingView analysis by MasterAnanda describes PENGU as having spent an extended period consolidating after its earlier decline. The analysis interprets the rising long-term support structure as a potential foundation for another bullish cycle, although the duration and scale of any recovery remain unknown.

PENGU Bearish Scenario: $0.0065 Support Remains Important

Despite the bullish SuperTrend flip, PENGU has not confirmed a sustained breakout from its broader consolidation pattern. Failure to overcome descending resistance could leave the token vulnerable to another pullback.

The four-day chart identifies $0.0065 as an important potential support area. A decline toward this level would indicate that sellers had regained control of the short-term trend. If support breaks, the $0.0050–$0.0037 region becomes a lower zone to monitor, according to the supplied chart analysis.

A convincing bearish signal would involve a close below ascending trendline support, preferably accompanied by rising selling volume. Such a move would weaken the argument that PENGU is establishing progressively higher lows.

Broader market conditions also matter. A decline in Bitcoin or a wider retreat across speculative crypto assets could increase selling pressure on PENGU, regardless of its individual technical indicators. Traders should therefore assess the SuperTrend signal alongside price structure, volume, and market direction rather than relying on one indicator.

Pudgy Penguins Fundamentals Add Context to PENGU Price Prediction

PENGU is the token associated with Pudgy Penguins, a consumer brand that developed from a non-fungible token (NFT) collection into a business spanning digital collectibles, toys, and merchandise. Its retail presence, including products sold through Walmart and Target, provides a broader brand context beyond crypto trading.

However, brand recognition does not necessarily translate into sustained token demand. PENGU’s price remains sensitive to cryptocurrency market sentiment, trading activity, and investors’ willingness to hold speculative assets.

Pudgy Penguins (PENGU) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

A significant development for the wider Pudgy Penguins ecosystem came in October 2026, when Igloo announced plans to shut down its Abstract Ethereum layer-2 network on December 15. The Block reported that the decision was followed by challenges, including stagnant growth, limited liquidity, and insufficient revenue to support continued operations. The company also decided against launching a token to finance the network.

The closure introduces a separate business consideration for the ecosystem, although it does not by itself determine PENGU’s short-term price direction. Investors will need to distinguish developments affecting the brand’s broader business strategy from signals generated by the token’s trading chart.

Final Thoughts

PENGU’s bullish SuperTrend flip near $0.0081 has put a potential recovery toward $0.013 in focus. Ali Charts’ reference to previous TD Sequential signals provides historical context, while the symmetrical triangle and higher-low structure offer additional technical levels to monitor.

For the bullish case to strengthen, PENGU would need to clear initial resistance at $0.0105, followed by the $0.0127 area. A sustained move above these levels could bring $0.013 and then $0.015 into focus. Stronger volume and a successful retest of broken resistance would provide more convincing evidence of a breakout.

The bearish alternative remains valid if PENGU fails to overcome descending resistance or breaks below its rising support structure. In that case, $0.0065 could become a key downside level, with $0.0050–$0.0037 representing a lower potential support zone.

The proposed 70% rally remains a conditional scenario, not a confirmed forecast. PENGU’s next directional move will depend on whether buyers can turn the latest momentum signal into a sustained breakout while broader crypto market conditions remain supportive.

The post Meta Shares Go Onchain: $META Launches on Solana With 24/7 Trading and 1:1 Redemption appeared first on Cryp...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The Meta Platforms tokenized shares have gone live on Solana under ticker $META.
  • The token is issued by Backpack Securities and brought onto chain by Sunrise, for 24/7 trading.
  • Users who qualify will be able to exchange $META to obtain conventional Meta shares via the Backpack at 1:1 value.

Crypto users can now tokenize their exposure to a major U.S. public company, as Meta Platforms stock moves to Solana. Meta Platforms’ shares are listed under the same ticker on the Nasdaq as the new $META token, issued by Backpack Securities.

  • Tokenized Meta Shares Enter Solana Markets
  • $META Can Move Between Onchain and Brokerage Form
    • 24/7 Trading Pushes Tokenized Stocks Beyond Market Hours
    • Solana Expands Its Tokenized Equity Market

Tokenized Meta Shares Enter Solana Markets

Solana announced that $META had gone live through Sunrise, expanding the network’s growing market for tokenized equities. Unlike a standard trading hour, the token will have unrestricted trading hours, supported by a collator from Meta Platforms stock.

BREAKING: $META is live on Solana via @sunrise, issued by @Backpack Securities https://t.co/stdJSQNkOJ

— Solana (@solana) October 21, 2026

Backpack states that each token is equivalent to one META share and can be used on its securities exchange as 1:1 redemptions; subject to eligibility and verification of accounts.

The Solana token that has been featured most prominently is the META aH6MMZZgy2CTEJq3QdNi7AFVTV3NxHFBfFgLEDd token. The Backpack-issued META token is currently listed in a Solana token directory to represent a handful of tokens representing Meta.
